title: Jeremiyah Love Press Conference 8.14.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Jeremiah first taste of preseason action was it kind of what you wanted and expected it for it to be? >> Yeah. Yeah, honestly it was a lot more fun than I expected it to be. Just being out there with my guys. I already knew it was going to be fun, but you know, beginning of the you know, just compete, you know, against some other great guys can compete against another team. Um, it's really it's really nice. It's fun. Real fun. >> Did you expect to get those double digit touches in this game? >> I didn't, but you know, ball is ball. I mean, I welcome it. You know, I got a little bit of a groove. Kind of wish I would have played just a tad bit longer, but I think I played enough for people to see. >> [laughter] >> Mike said that he felt like our said he felt like in the beginning of camp you were a little bit hoppy and now you're you're more grounded. What does that feel like actually for you on the field being more grounded and less hoppy? >> Yeah. So, when I first, you know, I obviously got here, um, still was kind of in my college ways. I would do a lot of jump cuts, like kind of a lot of hezies. Um, but now I'm a lot more grounded. Like I'm more patient. You know, I keep my feet on the ground more. So, like the second that hole opens up, I got my feet in the ground already. I can shoot through it. So, um, I think that's what coach LaFleur is talking about cuz I've been intentionally trying to change that. Um, and it's it's gotten a lot better. Kind of showed that today. Some holes opened up. First run got some yards, but yeah, it's going pretty good. >> Why is that more important at the NFL level than it is in college? >> Cuz it's you're playing against guys [clears throat] that when they see a hole that hole closes very fast and if you're hopping around in the backfield, that hole may be open for 1 second. If your feet are already in the ground, you got a little bit of a better chance to actually explode through that hole, and get more yards. So, that's the difference between college and the NFL. You know, things just happen a lot faster, so you got to be more prepared to take advantage of that opportunity. >> You mentioned how much you were looking forward to playing in the Hall of Fame game. Obviously, that didn't happen. So, what was the level of anticipation like tonight knowing you got to come out here and you know, get this much run? >> Yeah, I was shooting the whole day I was just trying to get myself in the right mindset, you know, that I'm actually going out there and I'm going to play, you know, a game. Um and I was just happy, you know, I was excited to go out there and and play with my guys, put on, you know, shoulder pads, my my uniform, helmet, you know, and represent the Cardinals and represent the name on the back of my jersey. It was it was very exciting and I looked forward I was looking forward to it literally the whole day and the day before and it was it was just a great event out there. >> Do you just is things kind of build for you when you're carrying the football? The more they kind of feed you the more Did it take a little while to get going? >> I would say today, um that's kind of what it was because on my first carry, you know, I was just trying to feel it out, you know, trying to see how guys tackle, trying to see how guys move and as the game just kept going, um I was getting a lot more comfortable. Like I was a little tense at first, but then I was, you know, starting to play a little bit more free. and I think the next time I step foot on the field like I'm I'll be able to play like my usual self, like I play as free as I want cuz I know what to expect. But, yeah. >> Do you Do you feel a little bit more >> out here today? I saw you had a moment with your dad pregame. >> Just two. My mom and dad came down and supported me. Um they been to every single game. They ain't missed a game since I've been in college, so uh yeah, there was just them two. >> What's your at the second level? Do you feel that freedom, that kind of not thinking it? It just looks like you're playing so fast out there once you get to the >> second level and you're against a linebacker or corner or safety. >> definitely I feel that, you know, like my instincts kind of just take over cuz you know, as a running back we're taught to, you know, first level, you know, you got your reads, but once you get to the second level let your instincts take over, let your natural play style take over and uh my definitely felt that, you know, whenever I got to the second level got to go against a backer or safety or corner, you know, those instincts just kicked in and allowed me to do some pretty good stuff. >> Where's your comfort at in the receiving game right now compared to maybe a couple weeks ago early in camp? >> Um I'm very comfortable. You know, um whenever I just I mean, I feel the most comfortable when I get out in the [snorts] space whether I'm running the ball or whether you know, I line up out in the slot or you know, they just free release me from the backfield last one I feel the most free. Um so like whenever I'm out there, we had a couple opportunities this game um where I was out there. Nobody was really one on one with me. It was just they dropped back in zone. So like sit or you know, break in and catch the ball. Get vertical. Um but I feel very comfortable when it comes to the passing game and receiving game. >> You We know you're You were just talking about having your feet on the ground and continuing with that. So how do you kind of have that balance then between trying to do the hurdle like you did uh for that 15-yard gain? Like what kind of runs through your mind versus the options to try to run through somebody? >> Yeah. Um it's it's all just instinct. You know, whenever I get to the second level I'm not really thinking. My body's just moving. So the hurdles kind of just come. It's not nothing that's just like pre-planned. It's just like uh I see a guy come to tackle me low, my body just moves and I just act. So second level stuff like it's just pure instinct, but first level is you know, I'm following my reads, trying to be detailed. yeah.

title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 8.13.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: All right. Um, just some injuries from the game. Chase Basantis obviously left with the knee. Um, Jameson Gears ended up right there in kind of that last little sequence. Ended up having a thumb and then uh Jeremiah Love had the ankle. Um, could have returned if if we needed him to. So, he's he's fine. [snorts] >> What does the scenario look like for Chase? >> Uh, not good. So, we got to run some more tests, but uh but you know, I'd say not good right now, but we got we got to run the run the test. So, does it look like an ACL? >> I I would that'd be too early to tell right now. I mean, because they obviously have to do the MRI and stuff like that, but um you know, there's there's there's definitely something down there over there. It's ACL, MCL, but we'll we'll know more tomorrow and then um obviously I'll be meeting with you guys on uh on Saturday. >> And [snorts] Jeremiah, are you expecting that practice? >> Yeah, I would think so. I mean, based off of, you know, just our conversations, but again, you never know. It's it's like one of those things that maybe tomorrow it's a little more sore than than the next. So, we'll we'll take that day by day. But again, he was I mean, just talking to him in there, he was he was good and you know, excited and happy to be out there playing. >> It seemed like from from where we were that the offense was just in such a [snorts] rhythm. Obviously, there were not many in the first two quarterbacks. Did it feel like that for you on the sidelines? >> No, it felt like we were had two false starts in the first drive and, you know, and um kind of maybe got bailed out a little bit on a on a third down with a PI, you know. So again, we're we're always going to be process driven over results. And I know we got the results, but there's a lot to clean up. And then I can flip it. They did some good stuff. There's no doubt. And I liked how the quarterbacks kept it in play. Called some crap plays where they were able to, you know, whether extend or just get it done to the checkown. So um there was some good stuff, but still operationally like we got a lot a long way to go. >> What did you see after you got after the 50 yardd line on that drive? You cash in with Martin Harrison Jr. touchdown. What did you see post that DPI drew? Yeah, I thought there was uh you know, good execution outside of the the false start. You know, we ended up having on the right side right there, but uh I thought the the runs were going where they were supposed to go. Um the keeper, you know, I mean that was that wasn't the first read. Um it was an incredible throw. I don't know if you guys I mean my vantage point was I said save those for September, dude. So, um but no, I thought they executed well uh when that ball was snap, but again, it's just some of that pre- snap stuff that that absolutely kills you. And if you want to be the uh the offense and the team that that we want to be, um you know, we got to clean that up. >> I know that I know that you are going to probably be a little harsher on yourself and the offense given your background and everything, but it does feel like things have [snorts] clicked to a point. Do you do are you are you giving yourself any credit for [snorts] what this offense looks like? Because it looks a lot better than it had. >> I I give the guys credit for executing when the ball's being snapped. I mean, it's it's guys, it is the preseason, you know, and and but with that being said, being where your feet are and and handling your day like um you know, good good little window right there, but again, stuff to clean up for sure on in all three phases and then we're right back to work on Saturday and it's it's back to camp. Like this is not we didn't break camp just cuz we left the wig long. >> What popped up with Carson and what is the concern level with him? >> Yeah, he uh tough dude. Um no concern level really. uh if this would have been flag football or seven on seven, we would have trotted him out there and and he could have thrown, but he just had discomfort and um you know, it's kind of one of those things. I was actually talking to Stafford about it and it was like one of those things that sometimes a few days later it kind of feels a little bit worse. So, being the preseason um just didn't want to risk it. I know it was kind of a bummer for for our fan base and you guys and and me and all of us cuz we wanted we want to see these guys out there and uh but it was what it was and we thought that was in the best interest to um you know make sure that we sat him back. >> Jeremiah gets 14 touches. That right around where you wanted him to be and what were your main >> Yeah, I was I was hoping to get double digits whether it be you know couple catches and and some runs so um that he got the the 14 right there. I wasn't really sure because I mean we only had the three drives in the first half and so it was uh you know I I didn't know where that thing was going to go. Like we get through two drives and there's like six minutes to go in the second quarter. It's crazy. Fast preseason game in the first half. Um so but to answer your question, not trying to be too longwinded with it like where like where he was at with the touches. >> I know you need to see you need to see tape and stuff. Did you feel like I know the first drive probably didn't go the way you wanted defensively, but it felt like they made some plays beyond that. Do you feel that way? >> Yeah, you're right. And and that's probably going to be a common answer for me in terms I got to see the tape with the defense because even though I am paying attention to it. Um, you know, we're we're gathering our thoughts and I'm looking at the tablet and stuff like that. So, it's hard for me to really, you know, see. I know there was some tackling issues and stuff like that. We'll see how many it really was. Maybe it just was, you know, one of the long runs and and it wasn't the rest. So, but got to see the tape and um, you know, we'll be watching it here in about the next hour. Has the [snorts] pass coverage been a concern at all for you throughout camp and then the two preseason games? >> Um, no. I mean, it's it's like one of those things like when there's all these different guys playing like to to be able to get in a rhythm like the preseason's tough. I mean, for everybody, all 32 teams, because you [snorts] when you play 60 65 snaps, you naturally just kind of in it, right? You're you're in that rhythm and um trotted some of those guys out there for the first time this year and and with, you know, live bullets. So, um, stuff that we'll always be paying attention to, but you know, I would say not a concern. >> It seems [snorts] like you guys have made it a focus to use Jeremiah as a receiver. [clears throat] Where do you feel like you can benefit your passing game that way? >> Well, if if you have a back that um can run routes out of the back field, you typically have favorable matchups. Um, I mean there's obviously certain linebackers that are really good at cover guys, but like if you got a guy that you feel is pretty dynamic, um, you know, that can obviously be a pretty big weapon for you. So, uh, now when you do that, you get a little bit looser in protection cuz obviously he's not into the protection. So, you I mean, there's a give and take to the whole thing. But, uh, yeah, I've I've been pleased with him. I think he's doing a better job. And I thought he he he self-corrects for a rookie as well as anyone I've been around. What do I mean by that? like he was really hoppy when he first got back here in July, uh, you know, July 22nd or whatever first day was. And you have to stay grounded as a back. When you're on your tracks, you set your track, you read it, you know, whatever our scheme is, whether it's duo and you're reading that the the play side back or it's wide zone, you're going one gap at a time. Uh, but you got to stay grounded to be able to hit it. And he's only gotten better at that. I thought he was a little hoppy probably to start the game. And then I thought as the game went on, he's he got a little bit more grounded. And I've seen the same thing with his routes and and when the ball's in the air, um you know, not jumping like if if you stay grounded through a catch, receiver, tight end, running back eligible, uh you have a chance for the yak and obviously for him when he stays grounded because of how explosive he is, uh he could turn some, you know, pretty easy catches into explosives for us. >> We've seen a ton of Jaylen Brooks and Simeo in practices and obviously in the games. What is it about their both of their play styles that these quarterbacks seem to lean on those two guys? I think the whole group I'm it's a it's a it's a talented group. It's a tough group. Um they support each other. Um it's um it's it's going to be interesting in a few weeks, you know, and that's that's the nature of this beast, right? Like I mean they're they're competing for for their jobs and their spots and and yet they're they're all they're all tight and it's um it's a credit to you know Tony the receiver coach and and just that room and the leaders in that room and uh so it's um it's been good. Is Baron Brown dealing with an injury today? >> Uh, yeah. He'll he's not I don't dayto-day if you will. So, and we just thought it was best like any of the guys all we say is is it better for them just to get treatment back in Tempe or you know come here easily could have came here got you know that and but he'll be back in no time. >> There was a point where it looked like Walt was a little bit winded. Was it just that just >> I think so. Yeah, I think it was a little bit winded.

title: Falcons QBs Tua Tagovailoa, Jack Strand & more speak after first preseason game | Press Conference
text: So, take us through um you know, your evaluation of how you did. >> Uh definitely not up to standard. Um not even up to par. You know, we'll start with the first drive. Um was it second play, just being able to catch the snap, you know, little things like that. Um, you know, I was thinking about it like what we put out there is not a reflection of the the hard work the hard work that we've put in the first two weeks um, you know, into training camp and it does no justice for, you know, the work that our coaches as well, you know, have implemented. So, you know, it starts with me. I got to be better with that. You know, I thought off of that play, we kind of got out of the rhythm. you know, we I I think we we could have had a a pretty decent play um off of a screen going to B- Rob and kind of getting getting everything going from there. So, uh starts with me and I got to be better. That's it. >> You just detailed everything pretty great. But how did you feel overall going out there? Not a large sample size for you obviously, but how did you feel? >> Yeah, I felt good. It's football. um you know, played some games, got some games under my belt, but with this being preseason, that gives you no excuse um you know, to be able to go go out there and put a performance like that out there on tape. So, you know, not satisfied, not happy at all whatsoever, but you know, we'll learn from this. We'll go into the meeting rooms tomorrow and we'll fix and clean up what what needs to be cleaned up. >> I know you guys always want to use the preseason to get ready for the regular season. Do you feel like you did enough today to feel like you got something out of that? No, not at all. Uh, you know, as I said earlier, we're trying to get into a rhythm and a flow of things offensively and, you know, there were a couple hiccups and, you know, we just weren't able to overcome them, you know, early on. >> I'm sorry to interrupt. Is this is this a setback just in terms of the competition? I know PEX is still got to get healthy and and that, but in your mind for where you stand in the competition, what does a preseason game mean for that? Well, I think to me, if it were up to me, I I'm evaluating everything. Um, so for me to go out there, I, you know, I'm I'm competing. I'm wanting to go out there and put points on the board, you know, not not go out there and, you know, we'll go three and out, three and out, you know, and and not be able to to perform to the level that I know I'm I'm able to do. So, uh, always looking at everything as a competition. Um, but >> yeah, I just got to be better. I I got to be better for our guys offensively. >> You were happy for your teammate Jack Stan. You guys went over there, got the ball, made sure you gave it to him after that touchdown. Why was that important for you to do that? >> Well, that's important cuz this this is his first NFL game. Um and and I don't think people understand it's not easy to get into this league. Uh whether you're drafted, whether you're undrafted, and as little kids growing up playing football, like it's always a dream to be able to play in the, you know, in the NFL. And so this being preseason, I understand, but like that's a big deal. It's all a big deal. And and as I said um earlier, everything's being evaluated. >> When you have the two kind of opening series that you did, do you have a conversation with your coaches like you want to get back out there or you pretty much knew from the start it was just going to be the two series in that? Yeah, I I I knew from the start uh what was going to happen um going in there and so, you know, you got to make use of your opportunity every time, every chance that you go out there and that's not what we did. >> Would you like to play in the second one? >> I love to play in the second and the third, whichever ones, you know, or or both of them that they let us. >> Why do you feel like maybe you guys came out a little bit flat? >> I'm I'm I'm not too sure. Um, but then again, I I would say it starts with me. I think that second play kind of set us back a bit. Um, kind of got us out of our rhythm and and flow of things offensively. >> Would you say you're frustrated, disappointed? How would you kind of describe your your emotion right now? >> I would say both. Frustrated and disappointed at the way, you know, things things happened tonight as we went out there. But we'll come in tomorrow. We'll see see the film and we'll move on from that. two. Did you have thoughts about James Pearson's news today? >> I I don't think I seen anything. I'm not on social media. >> He was suspended for eight first eight games this season. >> Okay. >> I have I have no control over any of that. Um, you know, but James is like three lockers down from me and we chop it up here and there, but I mean outside of that, that's out of my control, that's out of his control, you know. It's it's up to the higher powers. They just congratulate me. They said they they were fighting people to get it, but I'm glad that they were able to. It was awesome of them to do that. >> First time you played in an NFL game. Expectations heading in and what's your thought process after it? >> I mean, expectations. I just just wanted to go out there and and do my job as well as I could and I know that was the that was the expectations. That was the goal of everybody on the team and I think uh it'll definitely be they'll be good film to watch for for all of us and things to get better from, but I think we were able to do some good things too. >> Were you happy with the execution tonight? Um, I think you can always have better execution and you know, we we like I said, we did some good things and there's going to be some things to clean up. So, we got a we got a few weeks of training camp left to to get those things figured out before we start playing real games. So, um, but yeah, it's good definitely just to to get some stuff on tape and be able to see what we're doing well and what we need to improve with. >> Did you have any family come down for this first game? Yeah, I had my my girlfriend was here and her family and then I my mom and two of my younger siblings uh actually surprised me before the game and I didn't know that they were coming down and they were just out on the field and they called me out said that uh Griff, our strength coach, needed to do something with me and then they were there out there and I had no idea that they were going to be here. So that was a cool moment for sure. >> What was your first thought when you saw saw them? >> I like didn't didn't really know what to think, I guess. I was trying to like figure out how how they might have made it here or whatever, but it was just awesome to see them and I'm glad that they were here for it. >> What did it mean to have Tua and Penn get the ball for you to make sure you had that after the game? >> Yeah, that was that was cool with them for sure and they've been so supportive of me through, you know, this whole training camp just help Cooper has to Cooper Rush. Um, but they've been awesome just with questions that I have or stuff that they see that I'm doing like if I got to clean up my footwork or if I got to change up the way that I'm doing a read or something or like even just the way like with my mechanics use my legs and stuff. um they've been more than willing to help me out and try to get help me become the best player that I can be >> from division 2 to now scoring your first touchdown in the NFL. I mean, just what is that like for you to experience it? >> Uh it's it's pretty cool. It's definitely uh it's it's a little bit uh I guess it's a little different, you know, playing in an NFL stadium compared to playing in in a division 2 stadium. But, you know, it's it's the same game that that I've been playing since I was whatever 6 years old. So, that was kind of my mentality going in. But, I mean, just having an opportunity to to score a touch on the NFL game is really cool. >> What did the guys say to you after you scored? a lot of lot of congratulations and yeah, it was cool that they were they were all there to celebrate with me. >> What's the biggest difference from division 2 to NFL playing in a game? What what would how would you describe >> I mean, naturally just going up from a division, even division 2 or even if you're a division one FBS power five player going to the NFL, obviously it's just there's going to be a jump because the speed of the game's different. Guys are bigger, they're faster, they're smarter, you know, they they kind of I think they just understand like defenses understand a little bit better what offensives are trying to do and vice versa, too. So there's just it's a little bit more of a chess match I think playing in the NFL which um I I think is a lot of fun cuz you kind of just dive deep into figuring out how to beat the other team a little bit more in the NFL than than you would in college. >> Is it faster than you expected or what was it like the speed? >> Um I wouldn't necessar say it was faster than what I expected. Um and I think I prepared myself uh very well with just the details and things like that. Um you know and I came out there like hey this is my first game. I trying to leave a good impression. So I think I came out there um you know as ready as possible and just try to do my best out there. Zakura, this is an amazing day for you. I mean, it's the first time that you've played in an NFL game. Walk us through the day and just kind of the emotions of what this day is like. >> Oh, yeah. It was uh it was definitely pretty emotional just, you know, thinking back to like all the sacrifices that not only I made, but like my parents and and people who have helped me get to this point. Um you know, to make my NFL debut um you know, preseason wise was pretty cool just to you know, just just think back on all those times. And then um you know, just very blessed and thankful. Um you know, I was just praying a lot today. uh you know, just asking for guidance and things like that and um you know, to just keep me focused because at the end of the day, it's still football. Um you know, it's always a dream of mine to get to this level. So, it's pretty cool to go out there with the guys and uh you know, try to go out there and compete. >> Sorry, they're throwing a lot at you in this offense right now. What are you trying to focus on the most? >> Um really just whatever my role is. Um you know, wherever they want me, whether it's outside, inside, um just trying to be as ready for the possible for the team. um you know, detail oriented wise and just try to be uh you know, reliable um in a sense. >> What do you feel like was a really strong area for you tonight? What do you feel like you did well? >> Um I think I executed um you know, for the most part on my plays and things like that, whether the ball came to me or not. Um you know, I feel like I [laughter] sprung some other plays and things like that. So, I think uh you know, definitely some things I can learn from for sure. Um but I think I did a good job of just you know, trying to prepare myself and stuff. >> How' the job go? >> Uh it went pretty well. It's been going pretty well. Um, I've been having good sales. Uh, guys in the locker room are wearing it, too. Um, and it's it's good to see. Um, especially when you spend a lot of money on it, [laughter] you know, starting out seems like you spend a lot more money than you making, but uh, now everything is coming into fruition for me and sales has been going great. >> Awesome. Leading rusher for the Atlanta Falcons today for How does that sound? >> Sounds great. Um, >> I'm happy with the game, but it's also room for improvement. Um, I'm definitely going to go back to the drawing board, look at some uh, tape and see what things I could have done better um, on special teams or and at the running back position. Um it's never as good as you thought it was and it's never as bad. So um I'm I'm okay with how the performance went. Um I think as a team we could definitely could have done better. Um it's not the outcome we wanted to show um or come out with at the end of the game, but back to the drawing board. >> Yeah. Yeah. And you mentioned it's obviously not the result that you guys want, but how do you kind of clean it up from here and obviously take the preseason the next couple games to do so? >> It's on to the next, you know, uh we got to focus on. We got two joint practices coming up. Um like I said, we come in tomorrow. um look at the tape, look look at what what we could have done better and what things we did good and u capitalize on that from there and just focus on Indie >> those joint practices against your former team, right? >> Hey, I'm ready. I'm looking forward to it. It's going to be good to see the guys I play with um and coaches obviously as well. But um at the end of the day, we're going there to compete and I'm looking forward to compete against them. Um it's going to be fun. >> And obviously being here, you know, obviously hometown kids, is it cool to I'm sure you had a bunch of family come. Is that that element? >> Sure. I probably have about 20 25 family members here. Um um I got family in Charlotte, too. So, it's nothing but a 3 and 1 half hour drive. So, it's definitely uh good for them to be here with me cuz uh as I've been in the league and in college, everybody's had to travel hours away. Um so, it's definitely a good good to be there. And just for me, uh it's it's a real moment. Um Corky Kale, I played in the stadium a couple times when it was maybe the old stadium, uh whatever the case may be. So, everything was just uh amazing for me. It was just home, you know. >> Tyler, joint practices are always intense. Do you feel like there's going to be a different level of intensity for you going back there? Uh, I always practice with the same level of intensity. Um, it's just going to be more fun. Uh, now that now that I know I'm practicing against guys that I played with for the past three years, um, I'm looking forward to it. Those guys know how I am on the field. Um, I know how they are on the field as well. Um, so I'm looking forward to being competitive. >> You mentioned there's always things to improve. Obviously, you got to watch the tape and all of those things, but preliminarily, what do you feel like you guys want to get better at? >> Uh, definitely uh, efficiency. Um, it was times where we uh, ended up fighting the sticks. you know, first down, we want to come out there and be second and five, second and six. We don't want to go out there and be second and eight, um, third and 10. title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Preseason Week 1 vs. Broncos Post Game Press Conference | LIVE
text: Okay, plenty to clean up. You know, I thought it was great being in our building. For a lot of us being in here for the first time seeing what it's like in the building and I thought it was a great atmosphere for our players. I thought just was excited to be in front of our fans. That's obvious and we'll stay there because we got a plenty of work to do like I've told you guys. So, there's things that I'm I'm proud of the effort and and a lot of things that you know, guys playing into the third and fourth quarter that we're we're doing a nice job and then we'll watch this and and make corrections and then we can go to Indianapolis and and be you know, one game better as we get on the road for two practices versus a good Colts team. But we'll look at it and and we'll we'll grade every play and then we'll get better. >> Overall, did you think it would be sharper or just about what you expected for the first time out? >> Yeah, I mean, our standard for our football team, offense, defense, and special teams remains the same whether it's the first quarter or the fourth quarter of of the preseason game. About what you expected? >> Yeah, you know, obviously, that news just came down. Um, not going to comment on the length of the suspension or those type of things. James continues to do everything in his power to be a great teammate and and work very hard on himself in in and outside in the building and outside the building. >> Now, you know, is it at least easier to sort of like your plans for how you want to handle the whole thing? >> We've been pretty uh you know, obviously, we're anticipating a suspension, so we've been pretty uh intentional about how we've planned it. >> Yeah, kind of along those lines though without him, without Walker, I mean, what's your confidence level in the guys you have there behind them at edge rusher? >> Again, uh confident in our group. There's It's a good group of guys. There's young guys, there's veteran guys, so we'll work work through that as the weeks go on here. >> Was Jake Hurt came out after his one series, Jake Matthews? >> He's okay. He's dealt with He's dealing with something, but he's okay. >> With James, like what will the next several months look like for him? I think he's he's really come on and I think he's provided, you know, you're always looking for guys that can play the tackle position, and I think he's gone in there and and done his job. Good. Thank you guys. >> Awesome. Have a good day. Heat. Uh just to recap a little bit for you guys. Um, obviously didn't win the game, so that's always number one. Um, from a defensive standpoint, um, too many explosives in the passing game. We got to cut down on that. Um, some good plays by then, some kind of self-inflicted wounds. Um, you know, we had some penalties, some, as I would say, some penalties on some, uh, get off the field downs, third or fourth down, that extended drives, uh, that led to points there. So, we got to clean that up as much as we can. And I understand penalties are going to happen. I don't think that's a winning stat, but when you're giving a lot of penalty yardage and they're extending drives, we just got to do a better job. And really in the passing game, I'm talking about we had one in the run game, but kind of a bang bang play, but we got to do a better job there. Um, you know, in the red zone, I think there were four out of five. So, we got to, you know, make sure that we're trying to keep points off the board and again, some of those passing penalties were in the red zone. Um, from a standpoint of effort and play style, I thought they did a really good job. uh especially late there when we're subbing guys out, guys are playing a lot of snaps. A lot of guys are playing probably more snaps than they would play on game day when you talk about defense and then on fourth down. So, I was proud of the way they fought and battled. Some guys playing a lot of snaps in there. Um I thought the run game was pretty good. I don't think we gave up an explosive in the run game. And for preseason one, uh I thought our tackling was was pretty good. Now, we definitely missed some that will point out and it's just kind of technique errors to me, but um like I said for preseason one, I thought it was a pretty good tackling performance after the first time they've done, you know, we had those live reps um at family night, but um first real exposure against a new opponent. Um so that was good and we'll always try to clean that up because the first sign of a good defense is how hard do you play and can you tackle people? So, uh, with that questions, >> some of the mistakes that you mentioned that led to those explosive passing plays, has that been anything that's shown up in any of the practices so far? Is it isolated to >> I mean, you're always going to have some mistakes, you know, and I think that I think you guys will hear me say this a lot, and it's because it's the truth. Um, rush and cover go hand in hand. So there were times that the rush was uh affecting the quarterback and you know he got it out of his hand because we weren't on the right people or weren't on the right leverage or didn't get on the right people quick enough. And then I thought that the back end at times did a good job. Um and the rush didn't come alive. So those things that's always going to be you know an emphasis for us but they got to marry up. So it's not one person it's all of us you know. So, um, from a mistake standpoint in practice, I mean, obviously we make mistakes in practice. I thought a couple, uh, plays that we had we should have been able to handle a little bit better. Um, but we'll we'll correct it and go and go from there. >> Jonathan, we've seen Vaness and Cox both make plays in practice, >> then they make a couple plays in the game. Are they trending the way you think they should be? And is that a positive sign for, you know, maybe not having to blitz all the time? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, you know, the more um we can affect the game um with our, you know, our front people, the better. Um Lucas has been having an excellent camp. Um he's he's very a very versatile player and he can win in a lot of different areas. I thought the play I think the first play of the game he made the play in the run game. He could have helped himself out with his alignment. Um but made the play there and then he kind of wins on second down. That was good to see. But you know he's a intricate part of what we're going to do here. Um and he has to play well. And then B Cox I thought played violently. Had the sack there on the P and 10 the second series. Um I thought he rushed pretty well and he's a very good run defender. He's tough as nails. I'm glad he's on our team. That whole edge group though, I thought, you know, for the first time, you know, you don't, you know, everyone does it a little bit differently, but I'm not a huge game plan guy in the preseason. So, they were getting some things, different formations, different blocking schemes, different pass types. Um, I thought the the edge guys did a good job of just playing their rules and their assignment and executing at a pretty good clip for for preseason one. >> You said, you know, game plan. I'm curious. You had told us that you were going to punt on the question of how much you were going to show last. When Dom Capers got here in ' 09, the guys had never run fire zone stuff and so he ran a ton of stuff. What did we see last night in terms of because the blitz just sent Oloppelo on like that was that seemed >> punt it again. >> Upon it again, right? Uh no, I I think uh like I told you guys, I it's a healthy blend, you know what I mean? And and Matt's been awesome about it because like I said, there's there's no right or wrong answer with that. Um, but I want to get our guys comfortable with certain concepts um that we are going to use week in and week out. Um, now is that going to be a a Oladapo blitz, you know, week five? I I don't know that. Um, is the coverage structure going to be the same week two? I don't know that. Um, but they have to get when we need to be able to do those things. I do want to put them in those situations so that we can coach off of it and learn from it, you know, and you know, I was once told like a really good defense, they, you know, the offense knows what's coming. It doesn't matter, you know. Now, you know, we don't want to show everything, but uh I thought our our guys handled the menu um for preseason one like they should have for the most part um and did a good job. Jonathan, in the limited amount of time that Zire Franklin played, what did you like from him? >> Yeah, I mean, he [sighs] I mean, got us signed up, ran the huddle, played fast and violent. Three plays, so I'm not going to, you know, give a lengthy opinion on that one. Three plays is three plays, but it was good to see him out there. He was ready to go. >> Do you have a lengthier opinion on Cece? >> Yeah, I I thought he played a little bit more. Obviously, you want to give him some more snaps. Um, I thought he did a good job. I do. Um, you know, he covered well. He he was physical um, for the most part. His alignments, his technique was right. And he's, you know, he he uh he's a kind of a football junkie in a sense that before you send him a text about a certain play and his technique, he's sending you the text first, you know, and uh, that's good to see. But there's his he'll definitely learn a lot from this game um and continue to improve. >> Jonathan, what have you thought of uh of Warren Brinson so far in this camp? And I don't know if you talked to him, but just wondering how bummed he was that he didn't get that sack. >> Yeah, he had him wrapped up there. um had a chance, but uh he's a he's a big physical disruptive player, you know, with a lot of the athletic ability in his body and he can play multiple spots and I think he's going to continue to ascend. >> First time we spoke with Zier, he talked about how much he loves practice and just being on the practice field. >> How have you experienced him specifically in that environment and seeing his passion for that? >> Same. Yeah, he's uh that's why he he it was an easy acquisition uh because we do have a lot of good guys here. Matt and Goody have done a really good job of acquiring high football character guys. Part of being a high labeled as a high football character guy in my opinion is do you love to practice? Uh and he definitely loves to practice but we got a lot of guys that love to practice. So that's why it's competitive. That's why it's back and forth. That's why the defense gets pissed when the offense gashes them. That's why the offense gets pissed when we hit the quarterback, you know, not hit the quarterback, but um you know, play well at certain times. You I mean, it's a good back and forth, you know. So, um they'll be chomping at the bit to get out there tomorrow. >> Jonathan, this is a little off topic, but you had a game plan to play against Jordan Love when you were coaching [clears throat] Arizona. Now that you've seen a whole, you know, offseason program with him and, you know, three weeks of camp, anything surprise you or jump out about him that maybe you didn't expect before you really saw? >> No, I would I I'm not um I was going to say I'm not going to sit up here and coach a quarterback. I would say this, like obviously we know his skill set, game plan against them, right? Um can do it all. Um, I didn't know this because I was never on his team, how good of a leader and how emotionally stable he is. Uh, that's cool to see because it spreads through the whole team, you know, because you're going to hit adversity. Every series, every play is not going to be a success. And I do think there's a certain element that really good players respond the right way to that. Um, and he knows when he has to charge people up and he knows when he has to put a put an arm around somebody. That's cool to see from one of your from one of your leaders. >> Jonathan, what can you help me understand? I was asking Matt this too, like why does that one play where um Oladapo and Nixon have the chance to tackle the guy on the sideline, why does that go sideways? >> Yeah, we we just got to play with better technique, both of those guys, when you're hitting a ball carrier, you know, especially around the sideline. So, um bang bang play. We'll get cleaned up. Just technique issue. >> Oh, I was going to leave. Okay. All right. >> One more in the chat. With Mark Perry, what do you thought of the camp he's put together and just being able to to take down Frymouth there, you know, kind of keep him out of >> That was a good play. Um, [snorts] he's done a good job, you know, he's, you know, talking with Cam too. He's doing a good job on fourth down as well. He's he's a big physical fast guy, you know, and any any challenge for anybody in a new system, excuse me, is, you know, especially his positions, a thinking position, like can you handle all the mental adjustments and gymnastics of what we're asking those guys. Um, and I think he's done a really good job with it. He's playing a couple spots, you know, he's not just playing strong or free or boundary or field or, you know, the middle safety or the field safety or the boundary safety. We got all kinds of safeties, it sounds like. But, uh, um, he's doing a good job. I'm pleased with him. It was good to see him run around, make some plays. >> Whenever we talk to Hardgrave, we all remember, we all know what he did when you coached him the last time. with him finally getting kind of off the pup, what does the player and what does his experience with your system help him to be ready when you need it? >> If you ask him, he's he says it's a lot of new stuff. Um, some things are similar, but other things are a little bit different. You know what I mean? You just got to he just got to put on his helmet and get going, you know what I mean? Play himself back in. But, um, he's another guy that loves the practice and we know he can impact the game. So, it's good to see him back out there now. Um, I'm sure he'll get interlaced as we get going and we'll ramp him up and get him ready to go. >> That that is what he says. He says it is a lot of stuff, different stuff when we ask him. So, how how much do you think you've evolved? >> A lot. I mean, I probably a huge evolution uh since we've been here, you know, just I think uh you know, I know Matt made the comment of with the offense being what's Matt year eight now, you know? Um highly, highly successful, right? And I think he said a tearing everything down, going to start from scratch kind of deal. You know, we kind of did the same thing, at least in my mind. um the guys that I've never worked I've worked with a couple guys on staff um couple guys I haven't worked with um in my mind we tore it all down too you know and and truthfully it's because the game has evolved and adapted and this is a new team and we got new players and um you see trends and how different people are attacking you different things and you go back and watch the tape from wherever you're watching the tape from can we make this better and um I'll give you an example there was one and we were going through an install. This is like back probably in February. Um, and talking with some of the players and then you go back and watch. I remember it was like a Saturday morning. I said, I'm going to sit down and watch all all this one call, right? And it like by the numbers and the statistics, the call has been very good. And I remember like as I hit the end the last, you know, play, I was like, this call stinks. like it like it really does like I didn't like it, you know, and and I talked to the staff about it that next Monday. I was like, we have if we're going to do this, we have to make this better, but I don't know the answer to make it better, you know? Uh here's what the tape says. What do you guys think? And so that was that was like a staple call of ours for ever and ever and ever since I was an assistant DB coach, you know, 15 years ago or whatever it was, like how can we make this better? And so I think we kind of did the same thing. It just doesn't come out to fruition like Matt because he's been here for eight years. We're new staff's like everything's new. Well, not everything's new, but we have done a I think we've done a pretty good job of trying to make everything better with our players in mind. >> Thanks, guys. >> Okay, thank you guys. Have a good weekend.

title: Klint Kubiak Recaps Preseason Week 1: ‘Really Happy With Our Process'
text: Yeah, we're ready to go. Ryan, have the first question. >> Take it away. >> You got it. Hey coach, uh my question is in regards to Donte Thornton, do you expect him to return to the to the field soon? And as for Decameron Richardson, was his absence yesterday injury related? >> Uh for DT, yes, you know, we do expect to get get him back. You know, he's uh he's you know, he's been banged up a little bit, but we expect him to get back on the field and see some action in in the preseason at some point here. And uh D'Cam had a baby. Uh so uh he was excused. >> Clint, you obviously have a large number of uh UDFA players that have been playing at a very good level. After watching the film, could you discuss that UDFA class and maybe some guys that stood out to you, please? >> Yeah, for sure. Um you know, uh Keyon on defense has done some good stuff. You know, um you know, we got at the wide receiver position, you know, we got a few guys that have that have showed up between Chase and our and our young man from Indiana that got some good snaps yesterday. you know, overall, those are kind of guys that that come to mind. Is someone I'm missing that that you're thinking of that's on not on the tip of my tongue? But uh I think you know, there's there's there's potential for those guys at the at the bottom of the roster to show what they can do on special teams and and try to help us. So that'll be a a good thing to watch too in the last two games. >> Uh Clint, Fernando said after the game that he was going to go watch the video last night. Uh first of all, what does it say about his commitment? But second of all, is there any concern about especially with the young player information overload? >> Um that didn't surprise me that that he would go watch the tape. I think probably a lot of our guys did. A lot of the coaches, the way technology is these days, you know, you can you don't have to come back to the facility. You can keep your iPad with you and go and go watch the reps. but as far as you know, our quarterbacks, they're they're expected to handle a lot of information and and to process it all. So um I think you push them mentally and see, you know, see how much their bucket can hold and um you know, him and Aidan and Jacob and Kurt, those guys those guys can you know, they carry a lot of information. >> Good morning, coach. Um especially for these rookies and even in the secondary obviously with some struggles, those are first time going up against somebody else not wearing silver and black. How important is that this tape going to be for them as they continue to learn and grow? >> Very important, you know, and uh you know, we wanted to we wanted to put them in a lot of man covered situations, you know, we have some decisions to make. So uh you know, it's important that you know, we see these guys covering. You know, it's great for Jamar to go out and get that experience. You know, his first football in a year. Uh I still can't say enough great things about what he's done to get himself physically to this point. I'm really proud really proud of him and you know, last night he got back to football and got a few thrown on him, but he's going to be better for it. Um so we'll just keep improving. >> Hi Clint. Uh so Fernando seemed to kind of focus a lot on some of the mis- mistakes last night. Do you Do you think maybe he was being a little too hard on himself or do you like that he was he was really honing in on that stuff? >> Uh that's just you know, those to me that's the best quarterbacks I've been around are the ones that that are hard on themselves. They put the finger on them before they put it on their teammates. Um I think he played good football last night. He's going to continue to get better. >> Hey Clint. Um last night in the third quarter Arizona had a fourth and two where they picked it up right at the six. Um where you could have potentially challenged. Not not asking why you didn't or or why you did. I just wanted to know about your process. Did it Did it work out the way you wanted in terms of communication from the booth and the way that you guys had kind of planned to go go about that. I know the Cardinals hurried up and got to the line right away, so they didn't have much time. But I just wanted to know if your process went the way that you kind of wanted in terms of those kind of communications. >> Yeah, I think overall I was I was really happy with our process and, um, you know, we'll we'll keep improving as as these as these next games go getting ready for Miami. >> Uh, uh, coach, we saw Trey Sermon play mainly at right tackle, uh, last night. Kind of We know we've seen him move around quite a bit in doing practice. When when did the decision for him to play on play right tackle last night? >> Um, you know, we we have moved him around quite a bit and that's what we drafted him to do and that's a position that we wanted to see him get live reps in a game with. So, that was the plan going in. >> Hey Clint, so the number one thing, or at least something that was noticeable about the defense, was that the pass rush really didn't get going until the second half. Obviously not having Max played a factor in that, but what's, uh, what do you plan to do as far as helping out the pass rush moving forward as we continue along? >> Yeah, you know, third down third down was, uh, was not good enough last night in that first half and, [clears throat] um, when you're not, you know, I thought Arizona did a really good job, too, of attacking man coverage and, you know, they made some plays on the ball. So, the coverage and the pass rush has to work together and we'll continue to improve it. >> Clint, could you talk about that right guard battle? What you're seeing so far? Is it to you is it is, you know, is there a leader? Are they still tied in in a battle? Can you just kind of kind of give us your analysis after the game, please? >> Yeah, I'm I've been really pleased with how how both of those guys are playing. They're making each other better and, you know, they're making making decisions hard on us, but we're we're It also means we're continuing to build solid depth. So, um um JPJ and Caleb, you know, they're both playing winning football and they're both improving, and we're going to continue to coach them to improve them. >> Hey coach. Uh the Jack Besh obviously made a couple of nice catches, but he also, if you're looking at the tape, um he he laid a few pretty good blocks in there. Do you look at what he did in that game and kind of use that as a good example for everyone of kind of a complete game? >> Yeah, he's he's a guy that, you know, he's been highlighted before in our in our team meetings as a guy that um plays really well without the football. And just just so happens that when the ball finds you, he goes and makes plays. I don't think that's an accident. I think that's the the kind of guy that he is, the kind of teammate that he is. Was really proud of the contested plays and critical situation plays that he made last night. Um so, um you know, that doesn't surprise me about Jack. That's what his character is. >> There was some uh missed tackles by the defense, and I know that you're not in practice tackling to the ground. How do you clean that up but still be practicing and and take care of your guys in practice? >> Yeah, major emphasis, you know, we got to you know, we got to get better there, and uh we got to get, you know, very creative as a coaching staff with how, you know, with how we get that done in practice, and we will. >> Uh Clint, follow up on Fernando. You mentioned you felt like he played a good game last night. Did anything pop um on the film about his performance that maybe you didn't necessarily see right after the fact last night? >> Yeah, I think uh the thing that's that's just stood out for me again is that we put a lot on his plate and all the quarterbacks' plate getting ready for this for this preseason game, and uh you know, he went out and executed the way that he does in practice. Some guys, they get to the game and you know, things change on them and the moves fast and they and they freak out. And he he was the opposite. He was very calm. He was getting the calls in. you know, he was seeing coverage well. I like the way that he moved in the pocket. Um got outside and extended some plays. So you know, I think I think that Fernando has uh had a really good week of practice and you know, the things that he did in the game are things I've seen him do in practice. So he's he's consistent. The consistency from the position is important and I didn't see any any you know, game day surprises just because the moment was a little bit bigger. He was the same guy. >> Plant, with your analytical nature, as you were looking at the film today, was there anything that pleasantly surprised you that from field level either you didn't notice or maybe felt was worse than the film actually told you it was? >> Uh you know, I think the thing that stands out to me analytically or not is is our penalties. Our we really hurt ourselves. We put ourselves in some negative situations and that's not winning football. You know, offensively, the fact that we didn't turn the ball over is is always good. You know, that's something that didn't stand out last night, but offensively um you know, you can't go into a a half of football and not and not score points. So that's we didn't we didn't help the defense there. We weren't playing team football in that second half. >> Last two, Heidi and Ryan. >> Hi coach. I'm wondering when you take this team out into Houston in a different setting environment for practices, what are you hoping that they benefit from that experience? >> Oh, I'm I'm really excited about about next week. It's uh you know, it's going to be extremely competitive. You know, with a with a really great defense that we're going to be going against, you know. Uh those pass rushers are impressive. Our offensive line's going to get some some great work being out there in the heat, a different kind of heat, will be a great challenge for us in our conditioning. Um, you know, this trip to Houston couldn't have come at a better time for our team. >> Uh, coach, based on, you know, Fernando's performance last night, do you anticipate kind of like the practice reps to change a little bit moving forward? Do you see him getting more first team reps after after his performance? Or are you guys going to kind of remain with you guys been doing so far? >> We're going to put a plan together this week and uh you know that's something that we're talking about as a coaching staff right now, but uh you know, I'm really whether it's Aidan O'Connell, Kirk, or Fernando, I would say all three of those guys deserve first team reps, but uh we got to go put a plan together on how we're going to split them up. >> All right, thank you, coach. That's all the questions. >> Thank you.

title: Jaguars vs. Saints Joint Practice Recap, Preseason Week 1 Preview | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: I was going to say, right, I wasn't going to worry about the opens, but now Joe's put it in my head. Hey everybody, welcome in to Jags Happy Hour. Brian Ston along with Jeff Loggan getting back on a bike here after welcome aboard. >> It's nice to be here. This is your show. >> Well, we Well, I mean, it's not my show. >> Well, today it's going to be your show. Well, >> you've got the tape up in front of you from today. >> And I'm I haven't gotten through all of it, but um my eyes uh were able to see the entire joint practice today, but uh welcome back. I mean, we used to do this for many years. How many How many total years did we do this for? >> Uh, well, we did it from 2002 until 2014. >> Yeah. So, 12, 13 years, something like that. >> Yeah. Let's see how much longer we can go. >> I think we can figure it out. >> All right. And we're going to do our best. Uh, the Jags figured it out today. By the way, we are at the team hotel in New Orleans where the Jaguars arrived last night practice today with the New Orleans Saints at their practice facility. And we heard from the head coach right after practice his overall perspective on what got done at the training facility in Meety. >> It was nice to see the the skilled players keep making some plays out there. Uh I thought Trevor settled in defensively. I think from what I understand we stopped the run well. There was a couple explosive passes that we got to clean up and look at, but overall great work. I mean, you know, had a couple little things, but no big fights or anything. I just It was good quality work that you can't simulate at home. >> Jeeoff, this is the preseason now. I I was talking with James Gladstone in the lunchroom before we left Jacksonville. I said, "James, tell me if I'm right about this. These joint practices are are getting ready for the season, and the preseason games are about development, finding out who belongs on your roster, who belongs on your practice squad, and who doesn't necessarily earn a spot." Yeah, I I think that the joint practices are are a great tool for coaches to I mean because here's the reality. The coaches have an idea of who they believe is going to be able to help their team win. And and when I say who, I'm talking a percentage, you know, let's say 80%. Uh well, you still got to figure out that other 20% and how everything is going to kind of fit. Uh because you don't have a lot of track record on that 20%. And so with the joint practice, what it allows you to do is it allows you to get work with the guys that you know about in a very controlled environment to where they're not going to be exposed out there on the playing field with somebody who's trying to make an impression and is out of control. >> Right. >> A blindside shot from a rookie linebacker. >> Exactly. And so you c like today for example the joint practice today the starters took I would say 65% of the snaps in practice today and so there were probably a lot of younger guys that felt a little off and that hey look how come I didn't get my opportunity in practice. Well their opportunity is going to come Saturday afternoon. And that's also one of the reasons why the Jaguars have been able to attract a lot of undrafted free agents. And this is kind of goes to the Rams philosophy where Shawn McVey and Lesne, they they've done this in LA. And that look, if you have a draft, okay, the draft picks don't have a choice in coming to your franchise.
