text: All right, Blake, NFL debut. How'd you feel out there? >> Uh, it was great to be out there. You know, plenty of stuff that to learn off of and then there's also some good stuff on there. So, you know, just being out there being able to get some confidence from, you know, being in a game environment and, you know, things that I can learn from and things I can take away and continue to workshop, you know, it was it was great. >> How would you grade your performance? >> Um, I haven't I haven't gotten to go over the film yet, you know, so I I can't give you a very comprehensive grade yet, but like I said, you know, there's some good stuff. There's some stuff I want to clean up just like any other camp. Did anything in the game, in the moment feel different than you anticipated? Was it as you expected? Was the speed any different than practice? >> Um, I just really tried to take it, you know, one moment at a time because it it really is like such a blessing and kind of reflecting on that afterwards just to be able to be here wearing a Detroit Lions uniform on an NFL field, you know, stepping into a game. So, I really just tried to, you know, enjoy every single moment of it that I humanly could and, you know, I'm just grateful. How much do you think those reps against Hutch in practice prepared you for today? >> Um, definitely. You know, I was talking about it the other day. Those reps are invaluable. You know, if if I do something and it it works against him, it's probably going to work against almost anyone else. So, you know, being able to go against him and then also too, the reps that I don't win, being able to learn just as much, if not more, from those reps as well. So, you know, I've I've been so grateful to be able to get as many reps as I have against him. >> What do you think of Luke's performance and how he commanded the offense tonight? >> It was awesome. You know, I've built a bit of a relationship with Luke and just seeing him out there and, you know, cheering him on when he was in the game and I wasn't and having him back there, too. Just, you know, trying to protect for him as long as I could, give him give him time to throw the ball and, you know, he's a great person and I know that, you know, we give him time, he's going to make the right decision. So, >> what is the most important thing that you've learned so far from throughout? Maybe it's a technique thing or a mental thing or what whatever. What is the biggest thing you've added to your game? Um, I'd say like all-encompassing thing. Just whatever you do, do it completely. You know, like run off the ball. Like you can't be kind of hesitant. Like you you got to fully commit to whatever you're doing. You know, whether it's your sets, like if you're going to go really get on someone with your set, you can't go and get on with the first two steps and then kind of slow it down. Like you put yourself in a bad position. So whatever you do, fully commit to it. Like you can't be in that kind of in between territory. >> I imagine you built a pretty good routine for post and getting your receiver processing with what happened. So, what do you do after a game to kind of >> take the next steps, process the film, go to the next day? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I I'd like to watch the film on this plane ride, go over it, you know, any notes that I have, kind of write that stuff down, things that I need to work on, things that I thought went well and, you know, try and learn from that, get my body back as much as I can tomorrow and >> get ready for practice in what, two days. really like this. >> Um, >> I think there was a I don't know that there's anything super super specific that comes to mind, but like I said, just continuing to really be fully committed to whatever I'm putting my mind to. Don't don't be in that kind of in between range. Um, you know, I think there was there was plays out there where I was fully committed to stuff and it it typically went well, but the stuff where I was kind of in between, those are plays that I'd like to not have back, but improve on. That's the thinking for rookie though, right? I mean, some of it is just kind of a lot going on. Is that part of that? >> Um, I'm not sure. I'm not sure it's that. I think it's just really forcing yourself to truly commit to whatever it is you're doing, you know, whether it's like I said, you know, your your pass said, if you're really going to go get on a guy, you got to go get on him. You can't take two sets like you're going to and then kind of sit it down and be short on your angle, just for an example. Um, I think that just being fully committed to those things and continuing to work that, like I said, proving to myself that, hey, when I go and do do that, it's, you know, it's going to work. >> Josh, uh, really thrown in the fire here. Not a whole lot of time with the offense and in practice, but just what did you what did you feel out there and and what did you see? >> Yeah, I thought it was good to get out there and compete, get in out the huddle and uh, move the ball a little bit. I think um, wish we would have finished on the first drive, you know, not take a sack. Um, I thought the O line did a great job giving me protection. I just got to do a better job of just getting rid of it. Um, the defense gives us a good look. But, um, I thought it was it was good to be out there. Um, get my feet wet, get a rhythm of for the offense and everything. And I'll be excited about this upcoming week at practice to continue to get some rest with the wide receivers and get the timing rhythm down and um, continue to grow from there. >> When you have so little time in the playbook before you're actually thrust into a game situation, does it feel a little like backyard football? I mean, you've done this for so many years with so many different teams and different offenses. >> How do you kind of digest all of that? >> Yeah, I mean, maybe not like backyard football, but it does take a second, right, to get a feel for um each receiver, what they're going to do in different situations. And when you haven't had those reps in practice, you know, it's kind of like what can we do just to stay on the field so we can keep getting more reps and continuity, which I thought we did a good job with that. We're moving the ball really all two of the drives. Um, so, um, yeah, like I think, um, it'll be a great opportunity to build on the momentum from the second quarter, like this week at practice. We'll get some good reps, good competition, and then obviously next week, stack another good, good performance. >> I know that Dan Campbell, when you got plucked off the practice squad earlier, when you were here last time, he said he was kind of bummed he got away. What does it mean just to have this full circle moment to come back to Detroit and be able to have another opportunity there? Yeah, I think um that was a whirlwind for sure just that whole year and um I was I was enjoying my time here that year, right? Like just seeing a new team, organization, new offense and learning and growing. And so um yeah, I think um it was it was for me, right, I had the opportunity to go play, which I had to jump at. But now to be here and like jump back in, right, it was a whirlwind. I think it's Thursday, I got here Tuesday. Um but there's a lot of familiar faces, right? like some crossover and I think like at this point right any thing that you can grasp onto um for comfort really helps and so little things right like just knowing where to go in the complex you know makes it makes me be able to not take some of my energy and efforts toward trying to figure out where I'm at and I can devoted to learning the playbook and the offense. So um yeah it's been it's been really good. Like I'm excited. I've been a a fan of Coach Campbell, the Lions and what they've been building um really since my last time here. And so, uh, to be back really felt good. >> What did you see from Luke? I mean, you've seen a lot of young guys come in and out of the NFL. Yeah. >> He seemed pretty poised out there, didn't he? >> He was I thought he operated well. I know, um, the first pick, you know, was tough, right? Like, um, tight coverage. He made a good throw. Um, but I thought he he operated well. I think, um, a lot of times you get in the stadium and sometimes the play clock starts wearing on you and just the logistics of playing quarterback, you really can learn a lot about a guy in these situations. And I thought he did a really good job operating in and out of the huddle, moving the ball, touchdown at the end, I know really felt good for him to get his first one. We were all excited for him and so it'll be good for him to continue to grow. Um, you know, he said he's like it's it's just football like after the first play and all the nerves and everything and settle in, it's just football. Make the right read and throw it to the open guy and I thought he did a pretty good job with that all night. >> A lot of new faces on the offensive line. Just what did you think of the protection from Blake Miller? >> Yeah, I thought I thought everyone did a really good job. Um Blake um all the guys across the board. I'm still learning them, of course, but um no, I felt really comfortable back there all night. I know. Um I'm really upset about that sack that they that they got put on uh cuz I got to do a better job of getting ready the ball, but um from a protection and comfort and the communication with those guys and shoot long drives and them doing a really good job consistently in the run game and the pass game. I was really impressed with the guys up front. >> It was our first time to see a Drew Petting offense here in Detroit. Just any major takeaways? Where was your comfortability at with the play calling? >> Yeah, I felt good. like um obviously I've had Drew in my ear before. Um so he does a really good job with his clarity, his annunciation, you know, that that can be like the little thing, but it can make a big difference. And um yeah, I think uh I felt really comfortable and so um it was good. It was good to be back with Drew. I'm excited to see like this year like he's he's a he's a really smart offensive coordinator. He does a great job putting um the players in the right position to make plays and his communication is elite. So um I'm excited I'm excited to watch him flourish this year. to go back to a force fumble set. Are you at a point where you feel like we know about your motor, your high efforts, carrying control skill set to be able to make that play in the set? >> Man, it was amazing. We always I mean that's credit to coach Casey Rogers and uh you know and just just all going when you win the rush, you got to reach to it and then this when the ball is going to be there. Uh we call it a tomahawk on air, you know, just reach reach reach reach and then the ball is going to be there. And I'm just so grateful, man. And I feel like it's my first strip sack and to many more to come. But I just pray to stay healthy. I pray to just keep levelheaded, man, and just keep taking one day at a time. And I truly feel like I I I can help this team achieve what they want to Super Bowl. >> It's preseason, but you got Joe Burrow. I don't know what what does that mean to you, >> man? It it means the world to me, man. And I I I I truly truly prayed about it and I manifested it and I said, "I'm going to sag Joe Boro before the game and coach Campbell said the same thing." Um, man, I just and I kept telling to my wife, "I'm going to sag Jo. I'm going to get him." And when I just kept talking to God about it and it truly just it happened, man. I just first play the game, I got him. And then, man, it's just there's no better feeling than just having playing a sag and just accomplishing something for the team, man. And just celebrating with my teammates. I feel like I I in the middle of that moment when I got the sag, I I cried. I didn't know what to do, man. I I I literally broke down because but I had to go back on defense, you know? So, I was like I mean I I literally couldn't believe it, but at the same time I did because I saw it happening and I just like like I I truly just man I I knew it was going to happen some type of way or another. I kept watching film on them this morning. I like kept walking through my head. I kept like just seeing the play that's going to happen. I kept seeing what the offensive lineman going to do. What's his set like? How what what is he can't handle? How did he let up sacks last year? And I kept just looking at it and it truly it truly works when you just put your head down, take it one day at a time and truly just watch film and know what's happening and what how he can get him with. And credit to coach Shet, man. He made the call and I looped to the inside and man, I just got him. >> You got a little banged up on that kick return. Uh what happened there? You all right? Yeah, I'm good. I'm good. I just got my like my bag was the It's all good. I'm all good. It's just like I got my wind knocked off of me, but it's I'm all good. >> Sort of validation just in general seat belt camp, right? You've been doing this, but to do it in the game, got to do it for whoever was watching. >> I mean, truly just hard work pays off, right? Um I mean, you just got to keep stacking. Got to take it one day at a time and the work is not done, you know? Got to keep getting better. Um, I just got to take it one day at a time and keep stacking and this what I'm going to do. >> And I asked Dan this the uh you guys those first two series were against their first team offense essentially. What do you think that means for the defense? And >> I mean it mean it means the world with like the first first series we got three and out, right? And that just tells you how much how how much we train hard and we practice hard and man just I'm grateful for that, you know, and we're going to go back and watch the film and correct what we did wrong and um just attack it to the next. >> What is next? next on the maybe goals list. Is it Jane Daniels? >> Man, I mean, I just want to take it one day at a time, you know? Um, I don't want to look too far ahead. I want to do the best that I can in practice and I'm just going to truly just take it one practice at a time. Um, and then when the time comes, I'm going to do it again and going to keep the same routine and, you know, I'm going to manifest and pray about that I got to get the sack again. >> Luke, initial thoughts. [laughter] >> It's a great question. Um, still processing it, but it was a lot of fun. I had a great time out there with my fellow rookies and other teammates like playing NFL football being a kid from Mississippi. Like it's a big deal. It was really cool and uh the biggest challenge was managing emotions and I felt like I did that thanks to be to God, you know, praying a whole lot and relying on him. So um yeah, I was prepared and played confidently and and uh was it perfect? No, at all. No, not at all. But uh uh feel good, you know, and I'm excited to just keep getting better. >> Some new faces out there. What did you think of the protection on the offensive line, specifically Blake Miller? It >> was awesome. It was so cool to see him play. You know, we've been doing this for um you know, a couple months now here with being rookies and and uh it can be a lot, you know, emotionally and and learning and doing things. So, it was cool to see him cut it loose um to to bark out protection calls and just to see him play free. Um not just him, but all the guys out there that I played with, they're very very well prepared and u got a lot of trust in them. You know, wasn't many uh just, you know, sacks or anything like that today. And credit to those guys. I think they did a good job. >> You talked about managing the emotions, Luke. What were those emotions when you first stepped out there and and started going on that first drive? >> Yeah, I think the challenge is managing the emotions like before the game, like waiting around even the day before and like once you get to it, once you're there, like it's kind of like, okay, it's time to go. Let's go play football. But yeah, there's some still some excitement, some your heart's beating a little bit faster than a than a normal day. So, yeah, but I think it's just again trusting preparation, trusting your abilities, and reminding yourself of those things. and you end up calming down very very uh and and you get in a good state of mind. So I was I was good. >> It was our first look at Drew Petting's offense. Where's your comfortability at now? A game in with him. >> Yeah, I mean just I've loved playing for him so far. I love, you know, being in the building with him so far. Just such an encouraging guy he is and so smart. One of the smartest, if not the smartest offensive mind I've been around in my entire life. So I try to make him look good when he's calling plays and make good decisions because um I know good ones are coming in. Um he's a he's a great thinker, a great schemer, and um I enjoy him as a person. So like um it's been a lot of fun playing for him and and being around him. >> Early in the first quarter, six of 10 for 69 yards, you had the int. It just looked like it kind of bounced off Isaac's hands. >> When you have a moment like that, what do you take from it? And just talk about the learning experience and and how you felt with your precision in that first quarter cuz you looked pretty sharp. >> Yeah, I felt good. You know, I was seeing the game well. I was in a flow. I was in a rhythm. We had some big plays early and the the interception happened and it's just football. Like I lined up against another NFL team today who made plays. Um and uh it was their ones as well. So they're they were a good team, a good good defense and they're going to have a great year probably and and um yeah, just bang bang play. Ball popped up in the air and as a quarterback you always hate that, you know. So um yeah, I mean a missed opportunity sure, but good team on the other side of it and and just try to stay level-headed. Next play mentality. How about being able to get back out there at the end of the game as well after sitting for a little bit and take the team right down the field and on that scoring drive? >> Sure, just keep playing one play at a time. Like all you got is the moment and I try to maximize it. Um, you know, we weren't too happy with the score. We had, you know, put the ball in the end zone and like my mentality was go do that, you know, my teammates. So, we were excited for the opportunity. Um, take it one play at a time and execute the play whatever's called and and uh no matter the scenario, circumstances, whatever it was, like just go out there and do it. title: Tommy DeVito, Caleb Lomu, Jam Miller & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Tommy, just uh your assessment of what you were able to do and maybe what you need to work on as you got through this first game tonight. >> Yeah, certainly uh not our cleanest game on offense especially, you know, a lot of penalties, a lot of little things that kind of set us back, you know, when you have three or four explosives in a drive that get called back, it's it's tough to score that way. Um but there was definitely a lot of good that happened. You could tell like when we were playing, everybody was doing their job, you know, the ball was moving down the field, but like I said, just didn't start off hot enough. Um I think that a lot of the penalties and little mistakes here and there like they just need to get nipped in the bud early cuz it just kills drives. >> Tommy, not that long ago you were in in Baron's shoes. What did you see from him in the way he carried himself and did you offer him any any uh advice along the way? >> Oh, for sure. I mean, he definitely enjoyed it. He had some fun. Um you know, I tried not to fill his head too much cuz like I said, I've been there. You know, your first time really operating this offense against another team where you're able to get hit, you don't want to you don't have that red jersey on anymore, but at the same time like to enjoy it because training camp's a long time, OTAs, like you grind all that to be able to enjoy times like this. So, go out there, enjoy it, and just be yourself. That was it, and he did. >> Alan Siegel on the left. >> Tommy, in terms of your growth, how different a quarterback are you right now with what you were on the field today with than the first day you stepped in this building? >> Oh, day and night for sure. Um everything definitely between the ears especially because you know, being able just to know what the defense is doing and you know, that's a testament to the offense and the way that the plays are called and just helping me figure out what they're doing before I even snap the ball and it just makes that game that much easier. >> Tommy, you started tonight over here. Thanks. You started tonight two for five, nine yards. Look like the offense in general wasn't very smooth in the beginning, but on that fourth drive you led them all the way down to the touchdown to Kyle. What do you think changed as far as you played and how the offense played on that drive. >> Yeah, I think just stuff was going to click. I think for myself, I mean I missed you know, a couple throws early, one over to Mack down the middle. I think, you know, the juices were flowing maybe a little too much, a little too much excitement, a little little too much pace on the ball. So, really just taking some time to settle in, you know, like we said, like first time really bullets are flying around myself uh specifically because, you know, we have that red jersey on. So, it's a little different, but it's good, you know, once you get into that flow and then start feeling it and then the guys around you are playing or just becomes easy at that point. >> Mike Reed from the back. >> Hey, tell me quite a few handoffs to Jam. First time we really got to see the running game in I guess with full tackling. What type of runner is Jam in your view? And uh what do you think of the end of the game with the crowd and just the energy for a first preseason game? >> Yeah, Jam was great. Again, another rookie that's stepping up to the plate, uh whether it's in pass protection and then running the ball. I mean, he's confident in the huddle. You don't see him like looking around acting like he doesn't know what's going on. So, he's confident, so that helps myself and everybody in the huddle believe in him and feel confident. So, when we hand him the ball, you know, he lowers his pads, he'll lay the boom on somebody. He also has a little shiftiness that I'm ready to see some more and more the more uh tackling that I get to see him partake in, it'll be fun. But, the crowd was a lot of fun. I don't know what they had going up in that little student section, if you want to call it that. I felt like I was in college again, but that was awesome. They were rowdy, it was a lot of fun. >> Dan Watson in the back. >> Tommy, how how do you feel in hearing camp now with all you've been through as a quarterback? Do you feel like you're you're ready to take the lead, be the player you want to be? Do you feel comfortable here with Josh and everything that's going on? >> For sure, yeah. Like I said, um just so much growth from the first day that I got here from last year up until now. Um and so much more that I can even grow even more. So, I'm looking forward to that, you know, I really can't wait to get into this film, you know, because there was a lot of mistakes that were made from everybody, myself included, whether I was physical or mental. For me, like I'd rather the physical mistakes, you know, because that's that's going to happen. You're going to want to throw back, you're going to miss a throw, like that that's just part of the game of football, but the mental ones are the ones that I'm trying to like eliminate, make sure I'm going to the right spot with the ball, make sure I'm making the right read, and doing all this and that, because those are the things that like we correct in the classroom and try not to make those mistakes again. So, again, looking forward to it, but definitely a ton of growth from then until now, and I'm looking forward to build on it for next week. >> Final question? No final? Okay, good. Appreciate you guys. >> How's it going? >> Good, Caleb. How you doing? >> Doing good, thank you. >> Uh just a thought on take us through your day. Uh what it was like for you to get out there, get your first reps, and how you thought everything went as far as getting your first NFL taste of the NFL tonight. >> Yeah, it was amazing. You know, it was the first just a preseason game, but it was an opportunity for all of us to get out there and and go and play. This was the first real of I mean, we had the joint practice this week, so that was kind of like my first taste of, you know, going against another team in the NFL. Then the game today was amazing, go out there, be able to play, and be able to just play a game again. You know, we go through all these practices, haven't played a game in so long, so it felt good to be back out there on the field going against another team. It was just the whole moment of being in there, running out that tunnel, the name I got on the jersey, it was just it was a surreal feeling for sure. It didn't feel real at all. Still doesn't really feel real, but, you know, I loved every moment of it. >> Hey, Caleb. Uh you guys converted two fourth downs running behind you. Can you just take us through what you saw pre-snap to the end of the first play, and pre-snap to the end of the second play? >> Yeah. Just every play that they call out there, you know, my job as an offensive lineman, especially in those short yardage situations on fourth down, you know, we're just trying to move the ball. We're trying to get those few yards, and so my responsibility is the same with everyone else on the offensive line. We're getting that ball a yard or two, and so, you know, pretend we're in the red zone, you know, our what we say is we want to score with our man in the end zone. So, that's my you know mentality going through really every single play, you know, trying to get as much movement as I can on on the offensive line and getting those yardages yardage in those you know, hard situations on the in the fourth down and critical situations. So, you know, just going out there it's just my same mindset of every single play going out there and giving it my all. >> Caleb, about two-part question for your first game, who maybe was here to support you? And then the the penalty like that seemed close. Take us back through what what you saw on that. >> Yeah, I got my family out here. I got my wife, my parents, two brothers and my brother-in-law. So, they're all out here. So, it's awesome to you know, have them out here. I haven't seen them yet, but you know, a lot of their first times out here to Boston and kind of checking out the area. So, it's cool for them to be here and experience you know, my first game here. Yeah, and the penalty too. Just it's unfortunate. Penalties happen in the game. It's just it's illegal man down field. You know, we're throwing the ball. Can't be 3 yd or more down the field when they're throwing. So, I just got to be smarter on that and realizing you know, what was going on in the play, but it's just an unfortunate situation. >> Caleb, your first game action. Obviously, you said you just had the practice a couple days ago. What was the biggest difference that you noticed from the college game to the pro game out there tonight? Is it speed? Is it the size of the guys? Is it What was that like for you? >> I mean, you nailed it right there. It's pretty much everything you know, speed of the actual game, you know, how fast the game moves and then also just the opponents that you're going against. Those guys out there, everyone's on that field for a reason. So, they're all the talented players and everyone is is a lot bigger, faster, and stronger. And so, just compared to college, everything just moves a lot quicker. You know, really got to hone in on your you know, details, fundamentals of the game, your techniques, and all that. And really got to be smart out there. Everyone else is smart out there and they move quick and you can't think out there. You just got to go, trust what you know, trust the practice that you put in all week and just go out there and at the end of the day just have fun playing the game. You know, it's a sport that we all grew up playing and that we all love and it's the biggest reason why we're here. So, having fun is also very important. >> Gabe, I think after your touchdown series, that Mike came over and was saying some stuff to you guys as a line. What kind of things was he saying? And also, I noticed Will Campbell kind of chatted it up with you after that, too. What kind of things was he saying? What conversations did you have with him? >> Yeah, after every single drive, you know, it's kind of the same thing. We go back at what what just happened. You know, we look on the iPads and check what we did and what we can do better and what we saw from the defense and just all the things that you know, we can't really see out on the field. So, we when we get to the sideline, we can see it and fix it and get ready for the next drive. And then, yeah, having Will out there, same with all the O-line that O-line that they're out there who didn't play, you know, they're a big help today. You know, when we went to the sideline, they were all there helping us, coaching us through and know what they saw and you know, they're they're not playing, but they're just as involved in the game as we are. And they're watching every single play. They're coaching us through. So, having them out there was a huge help for all these guys who, [snorts] you know, we had a lot of guys out today that was their first game, including me. And so, it was a comforting to have them out there to kind of guide us through it. Thank you, guys. >> What was it like playing in your first NFL preseason? >> It was fun. You know, I had a lot of fun out there. Like again like again like like I said, as a kid, you know, you dream of this opportunity and just to be, you know, in this moment, it was it was really surreal, but you know, a lot of fun. >> Four tackles, two on special teams, as well. I don't know what your special teams background was, but how nice is it to make an impact in that area? >> It's fun. You know, just learning a lot on special teams is really important in the NFL. It's important in general, but you know, you know, Springer, you know, being the special teams coach like he he pours a lot of love in his players and just being out there and, you know, making an impact on special teams is really important. >> What did you say he challenged you a bit on special teams? What did he say? >> Uh he just like, "I'm tired of seeing you get blocked." So, I was like, um I'm not going to get blocked. So, that's that's what I did. Um you know, he demands whatever he demands the best out of his players. So, um you know, that's what he did. >> What did you think of the defensive performance as a whole? What did you think of the special teams performance? >> Yeah, I think, you know, defense is swarming around making plays. You know, obviously we got some turnovers. So, that's you know, pretty huge and, you know, a lot of guys feed off of that. So, that's what you see and, you know, first guy that made a turnover and then after that it just kept going on and on. >> How valuable do you feel like these reps were for you today, especially considering your start to camp was a little bit delayed? >> Yeah, very uh valuable. Um you know, like like I said, like just being an opportunity to go on the field and play the game of football. Um I love it, you know, every snap I had just going out there running around and um very valuable. >> Gabe, how would you say the speed of the game matched up to college and what you've experienced in camp so far? >> Uh I think it's the same, honestly, like from college to now like I think it's the same speed. It's just football all over again. So, my thing was just coming to camp, learning the the scheme and um you know, finding a role. >> Do you feel like you're starting to catch up? >> Yeah, yeah, for sure. Um just the game the my first game under my belt, you know, it's just it it it feels it feels great just to you know, go out there and run around and, you know, feel like a kid. >> Was there a moment where you soaked in the atmosphere, first time in Gillette, crowd, things like that? >> Yeah, like going out there for pregame warm-ups, you know, just being out there like this is like I'm in the league, like my first game. Um it's all it's all I dreamed about. >> Thank you. >> Yeah, thank you. >> All right, I got I got one thing to say. I am a little snuff uh a little stuffy up in my nose. So, if I keep trying to clear it out, don't worry about it. >> [laughter] >> All good. >> Uh [clears throat] just what was like tonight like for you? You got a smile on your face getting out there, getting your first taste of NFL action. >> Man, it it felt great. You know, just playing at this stadium, you know, just seeing all the fans around and just hearing all the great fans just cheering on us for me to just step on that field first, you know, it felt great. You know, I really wasn't expecting it, but I got to take advantage of every opportunity I get. >> Jim, um when you're playing at your best, uh what do you feel like you can bring the Patriots at the running back position? >> You know, I I feel like I got a you know, when I'm at my best, I feel like I got to continue to encourage everybody else to keep going and keep fighting. You know, somebody might have a a bad play, you know, the previous play and probably a little little word of encouragement could probably change his whole mindset and probably make a next big play. >> Jim, obviously uh nobody wants to see anybody get injured, but when a guy like Terrell Jennings is isn't there anymore, it seems there's an opportunity for other people to move up and get opportunities. Do you do you look at a situation like that and think, "All right, there's there's there's a battle to be had for to for a roster spot?" >> You know, I feel like every team got a battle. Everybody is battling from starting quarterback to the starting running back. Just everybody is just competing. You know, like like what I said, like everybody is cool, everybody is friends, but at the end of the day, pretty sure everybody know that this is a business thing, you know, and for me, you know, I'm just trying to earn a spot on this team. >> Jim, you got your work in the first half and Tommy was out there with you. What did you think of Tommy DeVito's performance tonight? >> You know, he did great. You know, it all boils down to practice, you know, during camp. You know, like what everybody say, practice make perfect and during the game, you know, you got to be perfect at it. >> James, how would you describe your running style? >> I'd say aggressive. Aggressive with a little bit of speed into it, but you know, I'm going to just do whatever I could do, you know, just to help this team win. >> Last question. >> That aggressive style of running, is that something that you've always had when you've been playing football, or is that something that you had to sort of pick up as you as you developed? >> Uh I feel like I always had that, you know, just getting downhill, you know, if it's a fourth and one play, you know, just getting that first down, you know, just being strong and just running through somebody else. Thank you. >> Hey Baron, um just start with did you have anyone supporting you here today? Who Who might that be? And what was your thoughts on the fans at the end of the game? >> Yeah, um so my mom came, my sister came, and my fiance came down. Uh fiance moved up here actually today, so she's up here now. Um today was awesome. Fans, atmosphere was great. Um you know, getting to play at a stadium like this um that we call home now, so this is this is really cool. Um and I really had a lot of fun today, enjoyed it. >> Baron, in in terms of your development, what things you try obviously trying to show you know how to run the plays and throw the football, but what kind of things you're trying to show with your to your teammates in terms of command of the the huddle, and and especially at the end there where you're run running some some tempo as well. >> Yeah, you know, I think that, you know, it reverts back to what we, you know, have been through this fall camp. Um you know, trying to prove, you know, a point to be on this team. Um you know, I think I I show if you know what you're doing, you know, that shows respect from the veterans. And so, you know, just, you know, taking it one day at a time too, you know, not getting ahead of yourself and you know, today was awesome, you know, getting to go, you know, out with those guys that we've been, you know, getting a lot of reps with. You go out there and go play against someone else. Um it was a lot of fun. Um but, you know, there's a lot to correct for sure. Um so, you know, it's just, you know, starting block for us and you know, we got two more games, so, you know, we got to look forward to that. >> Baron, did you have a moment to where you kind of soaked it in that first NFL game in an NFL stadium, but also uh how good did you feel about the the the drive at the end to set up Andy for the attempt for the game-winning field goal, were you able to accomplish what you kind of wanted to do to get you guys in field goal position? >> Yeah, once we got out there for pregame, um it was kind of a surreal moment, you know, you're you're playing at such a legendary place and so, it was it was really cool to, you know, be there in that atmosphere. Um and then, you know, as the game went on, um you know, we we just got to be better on first and second down. We can't have penalties that, you know, put us behind the chains um you know, that starts with me. So, being commander of the huddle, um you know, getting back to, you know, what's next, what's next play, let's have a positive play. Um but, you know, we're just trying to execute, you know, we're trying to do our job and, you know, put us in a good position. >> Hey Baron, uh going out for that potential game-winning drive at the end, was anything said by Drake or Tommy before you took the field in terms of just trying to calm you down or maybe find the right mindset going out there? >> Yeah, you know, let's take a deep breath, you know, it's just football, is what they said and um you know, at the end of the day, it is just football, you know, the ball's going to get spot and, you know, we we had a minute and something left and so, um you know, it's our our job to do what we're supposed to do, move the ball down the field. We should have pushed the ball further down the field for Andy. Um you know, but, you know, proud of the way that we responded, you know, we got pretty sluggish in the third, um sluggish in the fourth and, you know, finished off the fourth better. >> Thank you, Baron. >> Thanks, guys. >> Daelin, you talked uh uh about a week ago or so about Kevin Byard stepping up and saying, "Hey, after three practices, we got to start getting some takeaways." How pleased were you with what you saw with this defense tonight getting the four turnovers? >> Uh it was definitely something that we definitely like love to see. Like we say, it's an emphasis for our defense like every practice, every game like at practice it's always like we got to get at least two takeaways. And so like to be able to come away with four today, uh I think our defense stepped up in a in like a very positive light. >> A. Reese. >> I guess for our preseason opener, Dell, you don't always expect to see this energy at the end of the game with the crowd. I'm just curious what your impression was of what you saw and what you felt at the end of the game with the crowd. >> Uh I mean, with it being my third season like now like playing like a lot of games in this stadium, uh I thought it was kind of everything I expected it to be. Like I mean, I know how passionate our fans are and like how much they really care and they come out to support us and like we definitely love and appreciate them for that. So, it was everything I expected them uh all the guys with the shirt off. I thought it was pretty funny. Appreciate y'all. >> So, the work and this is it's a rough you you've had a good summer but to this point for a night like this is kind of >> Uh yeah, it's definitely tough. Yeah, they just kind of go back and watch the film, be better. >> What do you need to do? What specifically? Was there something out there to make that was it >> Uh like I said, I just got to go back, watch the film, uh build build from there. >> How much do you use preseason games as an opportunity to try something different? Is that something that played into any factor of the performance tonight? >> Uh definitely not trying anything different. Um this point is we're just going back to the basics. >> What happened on the potential game winner? Felt like you just kind of hooked it a little bit to to the left there. Did you kick it the way you wanted and just kind of give it a direction? How would you explain it? >> Um yeah, I feel like I hooked it a little bit. Um but then again, I got to go back and watch the film and see exactly what happened. >> And you obviously working with the new long snappers or anything with the operation that was different tonight than it usually is? >> Uh I mean, we we were working on it during practice. [snorts] So, it's just something that I got to adjust to. Lots of film and go from there. >> It it seems like you had a really strong camp, too. I don't feel like we've seen many misses from you. I think you got some good momentum. I guess how do you sort of balance that and then what happened tonight? >> Um yeah, I mean, there's just onto the next kick. Can't dwell on on the past. Obviously, tomorrow go in, watch the film, and then once once finished watching the film, turn the page. >> Uh yeah, I mean, I think just in my opinion, don't make it bigger than it is, right? It's just football. Um keep playing football, you know, try not to focus on all the outside noise. You just kind of show up to work and kind of grind and you know, hopefully it works out. >> You said the preseason was really important for you last year and just see it was an opportunity for you to kind of carve out a role for you. So, how much do you relish these opportunities now? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think um you know, any opportunity is an opportunity and then you know, these ones are huge. You know, you get to go out there and break tackles for the first time in camp and you know, tackle people and just so many other things that go into these games you don't get to do during practice and you know, like I said, these opportunities are huge for everyone. >> Do you feel like you kind of have a blueprint for making the team in the way that you did it last year or do you feel it's a completely different situation with with a new squad this year? >> Yeah, I think I think for me I kind of try to treat it as, you know, I even did this in college. Like every year is a new year for me. It doesn't matter, you know, how good the past year was or or what's to come. You know, I'm always focused on, you know, how do I at least for me again, it's like how do I make the 53 now and then in college it was like how do I continue to just always elevate my game. So, I'm to continue to do that, and you know, and not focus on any outside stuff. >> What do you think about Kyle's release package? >> Oh, it's crazy. You know, you guys probably You guys see it. Um you know, he's got some great releases. He's always switching it up. Um you know, I can't wait to go back and watch someone he scored on. I heard I heard he got him good on it, but uh great player, you know, he's going to have a great year this year. I'm excited for him to >> What is it You know, your receiving room seems to be very close. What's it like just kind of have that group and have each other to lean on? >> Yeah, it's awesome. Just like you said, like we're all so close. Um on the field, off the field, you know, we're always talking. Not even sometimes not talking about ball, but you know, it's just it's hard to describe you know, how close we are and how fun it is, you know, to to go to meetings and to to hang out together. >> Thanks. Thank you. >> Appreciate it. Thank you, guys. >> Um real football city and everything like that. So, it was fun for sure. >> You guys forced four turnovers. How did you feel like the defense performed here >> they um we preached getting the ball and throughout trying to count so far, and I thought we definitely did that today. Um so, that was what we did. >> Cuz like you set the tone early with that interception. Was that on your mind going into this game? >> Yeah, I always want to make sure I get um good ball production, stuff like that. So, it was good. I was able to go out there and get the first one early in the first drive of the game. Kind of set the tone for our defense for sure. >> What would you say was the level of urgency for you and some guys who are trying to find a spot on this team? >> Oh, yeah, I feel like anytime we step on the field like preseason, regular season, like you should always have a sense of urgency to go out there and want to put your best thing on tape. So, definitely. >> Thanks so much. Thank you.

title: All Access Giants Training Camp: Interviews with John Harbaugh, Colton Hood & Pat Ricard
text: [music] >> Welcome to another edition of all access Giants training camp brought to you by Hospital for Special Surgery the official hospital of the New York football Giants. I'm Bob Papa at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center. The Giants kick off their preseason 1 hour from now here on NBC 4 New York as they take on the Minnesota Vikings. We got a big show lined up for you. You're going to hear from Patrick Ricard. We got players wired up for sound. We'll talk about the trip to the Greenbrier. But to get things started as always we welcome in the head coach of the New York Giants coach John Harbaugh. And coach, you got the first game Saturday against the Vikings. How anxious are you to see these guys now going against a different color? >> Excited. Can't wait. I mean, you know, you work hard, you think you're making progress but you don't really know where you stand until you play another team. And I'm I'm looking forward to it. I really can't wait to get it started. >> Obviously transitioning from the Greenbrier back here to East Rutherford. Um how have the players handled that adjustment? >> I think they've been good. I mean, they're they they Greenbrier was great. They enjoyed it. They understood the simplicity of it. Where where you're at your you're in your hotel room, you you go to practice, you have your meals there, you got to shower back, you go to sleep, we hang out with the guys a little bit and you're right back to football the next day. There's no there's no life swirling around you. I think they appreciate that, but I also I think they'd like to get back home too, Bob, and be with their families and be back here. >> All right. So, as you come back to East Rutherford, obviously some intense practices during the course of this week. How have the players responded this week as you continue to install new things and work through situational football? >> really well. You know, we talked about uh there's an emphasis on a lot of things. Situational football uh down and distance uh the different types of plays, coverages, all different things that go into it, but we wanted them to focus this week on technique. We wanted to really make an emphasis on on their individual technique and try to try to work to make a big step in in terms of becoming a great technician at all the football things they do and I believe the guys have done that. >> How people handle pressure and operate when fatigued. Last week at the Greenbrier, you had the ball at the one-yard line. You ended practices on these long drives. Earlier this week on Wednesday, 10 minutes on the clock, fourth quarter. You're going through it. You got to get a first down. You have punts in there and then you get a 62-yard field goal to win. Is that part of developing the callus of the team is to see how they respond late in practice when you put these grueling sessions in? >> That's a big part of it. I mean, we call it the opportunity of fatigue. You know, you get tired, you feel tired, you know, you don't know if you can take another step and yet you've got a job to do and you've got an opportunity to to win a football game. And the thing about it is the guy across from you, he's just as tired or more tired than you are. So, who can who can discipline themselves, rally themselves, who can find a way to do things a little bit better than the guy he's going against? Better technique, uh you know, better effort, uh better execution, all the things that go into winning a play. If we could do that collectively better as a team, then we can find a way to win a football game in the fourth quarter when it counts and that's why we practice those things the way we do. >> Evaluating players, obviously, you got to get down to your first 53 and as much as you simulate game conditions, as as we saw in the Hall of Fame game last week, there's no replica for an actual game and we saw that two-minute drive by Carolina against Arizona. High-pressure situation. Is that an important component of this first preseason game? >> Absolutely. I mean, there's nothing like playing a game. And a preseason game isn't like a regular season game. And a regular season game isn't like a playoff game. A playoff game isn't even like a Super Bowl. You know, all those things are different iterations and levels and all that. But a game is different than practice. And getting in a game in the preseason in pro football and getting a chance to experience that and kind of, you know, get get the timing, get the feel, get your head right, get your mind right, get yourself prepared for when the regular season comes around. It's a really valuable thing. >> Coach, uh we want to wish you the best of luck this afternoon in preseason game number one, and we'll do it again next week in Miami. >> Thanks, Bob. We'll see you then. >> That's the head coach of the New York Giants, John Harbaugh. Much more to come here on the program when we come back. We're going to show you how the Giants moved training camp from here to the Greenbrier. All that and more here on All Access Giants Training Camp, brought to you by Hospital for Special Surgery on NBC 4 New York. >> [music] >> 3 2 >> I feel fast. I don't know if I look fast, but I feel fast. >> Welcome back to All Access Giants Training Camp, brought to you by Hospital for Special Surgery. The Giants had training camp at the Greenbrier, the famed Greenbrier, to kick things off here in 2026. Here's a look how it all came together behind the blue. >> How's everybody doing? Welcome to West Virginia. First off, I'd like to thank the Greenbrier for hosting us. I don't know how much you guys have been around, [music] but uh beautiful property that's set up for this. We're able to plug and play. You know, there's a lot of people behind the scenes that >> have been working on this for for well over a year uh to make it as easy of a transition as possible. Our Jim Feelin, Jeff Conroy, Timmy Sleeman, [music] and the equipment staff, Ronnie Barnes, Adam Bennett, the the training staff, Justin Warren, the IT staff. I can go on and on. Jerry Meade and his crew, >> to the fact that we were able to just, you know, arrive last night, lockers are set up, plug in today, the printers work, the film works. So, a lot of people behind the scenes, you know, played a big part in this, and you know, I know the players will appreciate it. So, [music] I certainly think there's some benefits to it to getting away from, you know, any type of distractions, whatever those may be, locally or at home. We're here to do football, and that's what it's all about. >> Jim Feeney, VP of team operations. Hotels, planes, trains, automobiles, buses, trucks, operations, we do all of that. We came to Greenbrier for training camp cuz they were looking to just get back to that old school bonding of going away for training camp. So, we looked at a number of different places, colleges, and things like that. This is probably the best place that had it all, a one-stop shop. Already had a weight room here, had all of the fields. What it lacks is it doesn't have an indoor facility. If the weather cooperates, it's great. If it doesn't, you got to make do, but so far, so good. I think we ended up with four tractor trailers, a flatbed, and a couple more straight trucks for IT, and to get our luggage down here so we didn't put in much on the aircraft. Our job is to try to make sure that there are no problems. That's what the the travel op motto is, no news is good news. So far, so good, you know, not many problems, not many things to overcome. Nutrition ordered, I would estimate probably six to nine pallets of water, Gatorade, Propel, and other type of drinks that they need to yeah have for the players. It looks like after about 7 days we're running low on Gatorade and Propel. And I can add this to the list of of things I never thought I would see. So, I was like, "Where are you?" I said, "We're buying out all the Gatorade and Propel in the city of Lewisburg." Look at that. Got a feeling this won't be our last trip. Okay. Guess they might get a little wetter practice. Coaches probably happy about that. Have to see a guy catch a wet ball or throw a wet ball. That's That's the one part about doing what we do. We don't get out to practice too often. And then people think probably that we're resting or something, but it's just it's a good time to get [music] things done. >> You can see the entire episode of the Giants setting up camp for Greenbrier behind the blue on the Giants YouTube channel. Well, the practices were very intense, and here's a listen to what it sounded like with Tremaine Edmunds and Jermaine Eluemunor wired up for sound. >> Hey, let's go to work today, man. Hey, play fast, play aggressive, and let's lead this group right here. Start with us, man. Linebackers set the tempo. Let's go to work. Dogs on two. One, two. Let's go. Let's compete today. Let's compete today. Let's compete today. Let's compete today. Hey, let's get it. Energy. Energy. Energy. Energy. Energy. Energy. Who, me? Physical. Come on, I like to hit people, bro. That's why I play defense. >> [groaning] >> Hey, GET SET. GET SET. HEY, TALK TO ME, BACK SIDE. LET'S talk out here, boy. Let's talk. Let's talk. Let's talk. Hey, talking. Hey, make sure we talk when I give it to us. Hey, let's go. We got to get off the front. >> Yeah, boy. Yeah. Let's go to work, BOY. GOOD PLAY, BOY. GOOD WORK, MAN. GOOD WORK. GOOD WORK. GOOD WORK. I'm saying we out here me and my dogs, man. Dogs on the outside and them boy coming up to hit. Yeah. G man, we here. Yeah. Is camera following me right now? I think it is. Okay. Yeah, I ain't telling no one. Hey, be mysterious about it, bro. Damn. I ain't telling I'm telling like a couple people. Yeah, just like be nonchalant about it. I'm going to tell a couple people, but I ain't telling no one on defense. I'll tell a select few. I ain't going to tell everyone now. I ain't dumb. Definitely not telling rookies. My plan was let me just whisper in AT&T a mic device. I ain't telling no one else though. Getting a good sweat today, huh? Your hands, B. Finish. Yes, sir. Big boys on three. 1 2 3. Big boys. Captain Maine. Good day getting better. Um You know, we just got to keep grinding one day at a time and I'm liking where we're going now. And I think that it's going to be fun this year. Much more to come here on NBC 4 New York including Shaun O'Hara's visit with Patrick Ricard here on All Access Giants Training Camp brought to you by Hospital for Special Surgery. That's not bad. That's not bad. I don't even want to see that. I've been a president. >> [laughter] >> That's not bad. That's not bad. Hey, hey, that's final. If you do you got to go in circles. title: Todd Bowles on Jalon Daniels: ‘Very Poised’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: [snorts] >> Evening, guys. >> Talk about Jaylen Daniels did in that second half and especially on that drive converting that fourth down and a couple third downs there. >> I thought he was very poised. He went in relaxed and we knew he could make off-schedule plays out of the pocket, but he played very confident in the pocket. He made the right reads. He zipped some throws in there. I thought he played very well. >> What was your overall outlook of the game getting in the win tonight? >> Uh just developing mental toughness, you know, a lot of young guys got to play for the first time under the lights and with referees and live bullets. Thought there was little jitters in the first half. They came back out and settled down and and and they closed the game out and they started communicating. And I thought they played decent in the second half. >> Huge game for Aidan Garns, the pick six, couple tackles for loss as well in the run game. What can you say about his performance tonight? >> He's getting better, you know, we knew he could cover. That was the biggest thing about missing tackles that we were worried about. He missed one early. He let the ball out. I think he let Breece out there one time, but he came back with a pick. He doesn't carry plays. The next play he forgets about it like a good corner should do. So, he's getting better every week. >> Peavy Williams had a bunch of tackles and some splash plays. Can you talk about his play tonight? >> Same thing like Garns, you know, he missed a tackle too that caused a big play going in there, but he came back and he's mentally tough. Uh they came back and fought, you know, they're scrappers. The little things we got to clean up with their first game. I was happy for them. >> What impressed you more with Elijah Roberts, the sack he recorded or the big run stop that he had? >> More the run stop, you know, we knew he could rush the passer. He's one of our better interior pass rushers, but him playing the run this year starting training camp and leading up to this ball game and taking double teams on the right way has been great to see. >> Has he been one of the guys that has maybe benefited more from more opportunities with with Vita out and A'Shawn being a veteran player that, you know, has some practices off? Is he one of those guys that is really taking the bulk of it? >> Well, he had pass rush opportunities last year and he got through some. We really think he's a very good interior pass rusher. I don't think it's because the other guys are there. I think it's because he earned them and he can rush the passer from inside. He's a very savvy guy and it looked like he put in a lot of work this summer and he came back to camp ready. >> How did you think Connor basically played? >> Well, Connor heck, he'd like to have some throws back, but I thought he was poised in the pocket as well and he made some throws and he got us down the field. We just couldn't cash in a little bit, but he got us down in the red zone and you know, wasn't too big for him. They zeroed him out a few times and he was very cool collected in the pocket that way. So, I thought he managed the game pretty good. >> How important was the pass rush tonight to getting that momentum and then sustaining it for the entirety of the game, especially in the second half? >> It was great for the young guys, you know, again, we're trying to develop mental toughness and the standard of how we play regardless of who's out there. I thought they showed up and did a great job. Highburn did a very good job and had two sacks in there and I thought the pressure in the second half when I when we needed to have it was pretty good. >> Overall, what would you say about your special teams today? >> A lot of work to do, you know, today was all about seeing who can play and who wants to do it and who can do it, you know, we'll go back and look at the tape. There was a couple kicks that got out early. They kind of settled in a little bit at the end. Uh, we got to get our return game going a little bit, but you know, it was about who can play, who wants to do it. Let's see what guys do under the lights and we'll start narrowing it down from there. >> Daniels has the mobility. We saw him run for a first down in that first drive, but you know, his ability to stay in the pocket and stay poised, uh, how important was that for the success for the two scoring drives tonight? >> It was huge. It means he was learning the offense, you know, and then he took what they gave him. He didn't try to get out of there too fast and he was calm under pressure and he let the system work for him as opposed to just trying to make a play and be seen. He did some very good things tonight from from standpoint. >> Coach, a lot of the guys we're talking about aren't just rookies. They were undrafted rookies. Jaylon Daniels, Adrian Gardner, Shaq Thompson. Does this just underscore how important it is to nail that part of the procedure after the draft? >> I mean, that's huge, you know, that's the part that goes unseen and you never hear about these guys. I think Jason and the staff does a great job uh doing the little things and after the draft is over, finding the right guys and that's hard to do in free agency with the money going everywhere and guys being picked by every team, but to find the right guys for our team and bring them in and trust them to learn the system and the coaches putting them to work and putting them in the right position. I think it's a great collaboration. >> [bell] >> Okay, good. Thank you, coach. >> Yeah. >> Thanks, Doc.

I mean, it was a situation where we were on fourth and five. We have to be able to get the first down to be able to go down there and score. And at the end of the day, you know, the the the game isn't over until those clock have 3-0 on the clock. And you know, as much as I was happy that we were able to score that touchdown. In my mind, I'm like, if we get that ball again and it's tied up, we got to go out there and be able to operate to be able to make sure that we win this game. When you when you're able to to communicate from a from a quarterback language and be able to say, "This is exactly what I see and this is what I felt." And he's able to be like, "All right, bet. No, I I see exactly why you felt that way. I see when you're watching the film." Like it's easy to be able to be a a play clicker coach and be able to go frame-by-frame. When you're talking to Z Rob, Chandler, and T.J., those three guys have have all played the quarterback position. Thank you. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Appreciate your time, Chandler.

title: Robert Saleh on Cam Ward's Growth, Nick Singleton & the O-Line | Press Conference
text: One of the things that was kind of an an issue for Cam last year, we've seen it a little bit in practice and again last night is that he looked good on the first drive and things were in sync, but then when things kind of got out of sync, it seemed like that there were multiple incompletions. What do you feel like is causing that and how much of a concern is it and how do you correct it? >> You know, we've um the the good news is going back and uh digging in on the film like every pass play that uh Dave's called yesterday, we've run in practice and uh you guys have been there and you guys have seen flashes of uh of Cam and the entire offense operating at a very high level. And um it's as simple as just time on task. You know, he's uh every single one of those plays he's executed flawlessly in practice and he's got to be able to have the confidence in not only himself, but his teammates to just execute, get your feet down, uh play with great technique, and deliver the football just like he has and uh you know, we're going to we're going to continue to harp on all the technique, the fundamentals. We're going to continue to rep things at a high level and um but it's it's just reps. >> Good morning, Robert. Uh with that trying to learn about this team and and what you've got in these players, where do you feel like you're at in that process now with uh 2 weeks of uh preseason still kind of left to go? >> You know, if um this past week I I I I really think that uh we had a really really really productive week. You know, when you look at um you know, both line of scrimmages offensively and defensively, I thought offense uh on Tuesday had a really great day running the football, protecting protecting the quarterback. Um and I think that translated into the uh into the game and so did the defensive line. I thought the defensive line did a really nice job with regards to the run game and um now the front seven and I think that carried on into the game. There's always going to be things to get better at. And um and right now when you look at it, there's you know, winning one-on-ones uh in the past game both offensively and defensively uh are going to are are always always for the history of football always been urgent uh matter. >> And And Hill played a lot of snaps last night. How how'd you like what you saw from him both in the joint practice and in the game? >> Anthony uh Anthony Hill, you said? >> That's correct. >> Yeah. Uh I thought Anthony uh Anthony showed up pretty well. You know, he's got uh One thing, you know, he's really young and and what he does have is is an immense [clears throat] amount of power and strike. And when offensive lineman get to that second level, he's able to dip and get under their pads and knock them off to get to the ball and um you know, he's he's continuing to learn. There's always going to be things for him where uh as a rookie he's got to continue to accelerate his ability to communicate at a very high level. Um but at the same time, I thought for his first time out uh live bullets, I thought he did a nice job. >> Hey Robert, um what did you make of the the performance from the swing tackle spot last night? I'm sorry. Two more weeks. And um so there's a lot of things that we got to look at over the next couple of weeks and uh but so far so good. >> Paul, go ahead. >> Robert, uh sorry if I'm repetitive. I think he had ample amount of time when you look at it and uh um when you look at the like I said, the play design. Uh every single play that uh we ran yesterday is the uh we ran in practice and the entire offense executed perfectly. So, again, it's time on task. It's building trust with his teammates. It's building confidence in himself. Um but uh but there's no doubt Cam is capable. We've just got to go execute. >> Robert, what is it about uh Nick Singleton's running style that made him effective last night and what have you seen from him so far? >> Uh you know, he's got great vision. So, um again, he's got he's got a lot to him. Um obviously, still a lot of things that he's got to clean up also, but uh but again, for a rookie first start, that's pretty good. >> Robert, I'm what you thought of Parnell Tate's uh night and what you thought in terms of how he did on separation. I thought our run game showed what you saw in the run game yesterday was really a continuation of what happened on Tuesday. And that was that that's exciting. Um and it it'll be exciting to see if we can do that again against the world champs, you know, and and arguably the best defense in all of football. Um and then from a defensive standpoint, same thing. I thought we did a really nice job in the run game on Tuesday. Uh held our own against a really, really good offense and I felt like that continued on uh into Saturday into into the um uh game yesterday. We all and all and both phases need to get better in the pass game. Whether it's one-on-one man coverage, uh understanding our zone uh uh the details of our zone coverage, which showed on Tuesday. And um and then offensively, obviously, the timing and the trust and um winning your one-on-ones, getting the ball to where we need to get it. So, there's there's always going to be things to work on, but like I said, th- this was a very productive week. Uh tough-minded team and a team that's going to be ready to work. >> Robert, with the the sacks that took place when uh Levis was in there at quarterback, how much of those were a product of guys not winning their one-on-ones and how much of it was uh a product of being in the seven-step drop on several of those? >> Yeah, it's a little bit of both. Uh some coverage, some losses in the one-on-one situations, but um um you know, credit to those guys. Um you know, they have a couple of uh really really good talent uh talented pass rushers. Um along the call it the back half of the roster, uh just being there a year ago. And um the reality is Cam still made great decisions. I think the one decision he missed on was trying to throw the corner in the end zone when it was a it was a hand-off read. Otherwise, um you know, when it came to his drop-back drop-back pass game and all the other RPOs or quick game, he was making the right decisions. Um and he was going he was he was throwing the ball where it needed to be thrown. But again, it comes back to time on task, trusting yourself, trusting your teammates, uh play within the rhythm uh rhythm of the play and uh get your feet in the ground and throw an accurate football. It's It's that simple and it's It sounds simple, but at the same time we've we've got to be able to go do it from and take it from practice to the game. >> I know you talk uh Robert about time on task and maybe this is something you need to talk to your staff about, but is 20 plays roughly the sweet spot in all these preseason games or do you kind of build up as you go on and get close to the regular season? >> We're we're going to build up. Um you know, uh hopefully and and I think our our ones ended up uh getting almost 25, but um the goal isn't uh next week 25 to 30 uh for for the ones and then uh the third game getting over 30. So we may end up going the whole first half this next game and uh but it again, it's all it's all a numbers uh numbers game at this point.

title: Keeanu Benton extension REACTION, why it makes sense, price point right?  | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you. The Steelers do have some news today. Keanu Benton gets a 4-year $72 million extension, $18 million per year. Right around where if you guys have been listening to the show, I expected him to get. Um the interior pass rush productivity at five and a half sacks last year. He's now moving to three-tech, four-eye, one-tech. He's moving further out. When you have this level of productivity and you're in a more aggressive scheme, plus you're moving out to an area that should rely on his quickness and utilize that better. Um you were talking about a guy that is really prime for a potential breakout season. He could have gotten $20 million more or more if he had a seven-sack year with the Steelers. So, this could be a really good contract if it ages in that manner. We'll see. Um I don't think it's a crazy contract because of how hard it is to find interior pass rushers. It's really hard to do that. You know, you think about these pass rushers on the inside and there's just not that many of them. The Steelers, you know, have him and Cam Heyward. They're working working on that, but they don't have a ton of depth there. And if they had let Keanu Benton walk after this year, their interior pass rush really would have been the only proven piece as of now is Cam Heyward. We'll see if Harmon can take that step. But Benton is such a pillar of this young team, of that young D-line, of the room that you're thinking, you know, kind of putting him as one of Cam Heyward's successors. Cam should still be around for the next probably two seasons. You know, his contract runs the next two seasons, but we'll see. This, you know, Ben's going to always have I think some limitations in run defense. But it's harder to find interior pass rushers. Interior pass rushers are at a premium. You can get five sacks as an interior pass rusher and get $15 million or more a year. I mean, Turk Wharton had one year at seven sacks and got $15 million. Um you know, this is a guy in Keanu Benton that's been on the upswing. He's continuing to get better every season. And so, I'm not surprised by this um at all. I think it's a good contract for the Steelers. text: A beautiful display of ball for the brand new Pittsburgh Steelers who are under the leadership of a man from Greenfield. Ladies and gentlemen, this guy is a Super Bowl champion. He's been a head coach of the Green Bay Packers, the Dallas Cowboys, and now the Pittsburgh Steelers. Fresh off a night whereby saying, "Hey, this guy might actually h be able to coach some quarterback a little bit." >> All three quarterbacks had all prototype nights for the Pittsburgh Steelers last night. Obviously, you've been a head coach for a hundred years now, but did last night feel different than another preseason game? >> Oh, definitely without a doubt. I mean, Aaron and I were talking in pregame about just how special, you know, that, you know, last night was, you know, for for the start of it. But, yeah, it trust me, it it's not lost. Uh there's reminders all the time. I mean, it's it's every day going to work. I mean, I I walk and drive the streets that, you know, that I grew up on. So being back here, it's it's it's incredible. It's incredible for our family and uh we thoroughly enjoyed last night just the the experience. Very thankful for it. >> Hell yeah. You know, there's so many different things you're trying to accomplish, you know, in the preseason. So, I thought we got off to, you know, good start there. So, that was that was excellent. And then, you know, and Drew had a a huge second half. So, um, you know, I think it's, uh, clearly a performance that we can build off of as a as a quarterback room, but this is a hell of a room. I'm really excited about these guys.
